daily_summary: 오늘은 AI 에이전트의 발전과 실제 적용 가능성이 크게 주목받은 하루였습니다. 특히 구글의 Gemini 4 Argon 에이전트가 마인크래프트와 스타크래프트에서 뛰어난 성능을 보이며 에이전트 기술의 진보를 입증했고, 동시에 Beam과 FLUX 3 Image Klein 모델 같은 새로운 오픈 모델들이 공개되어 개발자들에게 더 넓은 선택지를 제공했습니다. 또한, AI가 소프트웨어 개발 프로세스에 깊숙이 통합되어 PostgreSQL 19 출시 지연에 영향을 미치거나 Stack Overflow의 성장을 견인하는 등, AI의 실용적 활용 범위가 점차 확대되고 있음을 확인할 수 있었습니다. 이러한 흐름 속에서 AI의 윤리적 사용과 시스템의 신뢰성에 대한 논의도 꾸준히 이어지고 있습니다.

items.title: Welcome Beam: a 501B open model you can own, customize, and scale
items.body:
Beam is focused on coding and agentic use cases. It is for teams that want a frontier-scale model on their own hardware, infrastructure, or cloud, and want to customize it to their own use cases. Beam ships with its own dedicated open source Rust based harness that delivers the best performance from the model.

Beam has a native transformers implementation, as well as downstream libraries like vLLM and SGLang. We’ve worked with the Reflection team to bring you inference, SFT (supervised fine tuning), and RL (reinforcement learning) recipes for you to build with this model for your needs. On top of day-0 support in transformers, SGLang and vLLM, this post shows you how to run it, how to post-train it, and what we built with it.

501B-parameter MoEs LLM with 23B active per token. 52 layers, 256 experts per MoE layer, 8 routed per token. Text in, text out with context window of 1M tokens. Checkpoint formats: BF16, FP8, and NVFP4 Reasoning that can stay in context across turns (preserve_thinking), tool calling with a dedicated grammar. The model supports five reasoning values: "low", "medium" (default), "high", "xhigh", and "max". Response template in the tokenizer. Speculative decoding drafter model with DFlash2 Day-0 libraries: transformers, SGLang, vLLM. Full-parameter RL with Miles. Ships with a Rust-based custom harness. Apache 2.0.

Reflection is going to give out $10,000 Hub credits to the best projects that use Beam. All you have to do is make a thing, and share it on the Hub:

You could make a demo that uses the Beam model on Spaces

You could quantize it for your favorite hardware

You could generate a synthetic dataset for your favorite problem

You could build an RL environment with or for Beam

You could benchmark Beam and share the results.

If you build something with Beam, then share it on the Hub for a chance to win $10,000. All you have to do is build the space, model, or dataset repo and share it on the model’s repo page. We’ll collect all the links, select the best, and send out the credits to your Hub accounts.

Beam is a text-only model built for long-context (1M context length) reasoning and agentic work. It is a sparse MoE model, where each token is computed by a small fraction of the network, so it runs at the speed of a much smaller model while keeping the capacity of a large one.

The decoder has 52 layers with a hidden size of 5,120. Most layers use sliding-window attention over the previous 512 tokens; every sixth layer, and the last one, attend to the full context. That gives 43 sliding-window layers and 9 global ones.

Inside the attention block (both layer types)

The two kinds of layers handle position differently. Sliding-window layers use RoPE, since relative position matters most within a short window. Global layers use no positional encoding. Instead, each query is multiplied by a scaler that grows slowly with the number of visible tokens, (1 + (pos + 1) / 2048) ** 0.1. It acts as a temperature: the softmax keeps its precision as the context lengthens instead of flattening out. The implementation calls this scalable-softmax query scaling.

Attention uses grouped-query attention with 48 query heads and 8 key-value heads, with RMSNorm on queries and keys. A learned sigmoid gate, computed from the layer input, scales every channel of every head before the output projection.

The first 3 layers use a dense SwiGLU MLP. The other 49 replace it with a Mixture-of-Experts block of 256 experts, each a SwiGLU MLP with an intermediate size of 2,560, or about 39M parameters. The experts hold 98.4% of the model's parameters.

The router follows DeepSeek-V3's group-limited scheme. It scores all 256 experts with a sigmoid, splits them into 8 groups of 32, keeps the 4 best groups (ranked by the sum of each group's top two scores), then picks the top 8 experts inside them. Beam uses the same group sizes as DeepSeek-V3 but no shared expert. Expert outputs are combined with normalized router weights and scaled by 2.5.

Only 8 experts run per token, so the model computes each token with about 23B parameters. All 256 experts stay in memory, so deployment needs the memory of a 501B model but runs at the speed of a 23B one. The BF16 checkpoint is about 1 TB in safetensors format. The NVFP4 checkpoint stores most parameters in 4-bit precision for NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs, some parameters are kept in BF16 for accuracy. There are also FP8 checkpoints on the hub which are ideal for Hopper and Ampere series chips.

If you want to deploy Beam yourself, check out the vLLM or SGLang recipes below.

The residual connections are the most distinctive part. A standard transformer adds each sublayer output to the stream with weight 1, so the stream grows with depth.

Beam counts the input embedding as step 1. At step k it adds the sublayer output with weight 1/sqrt(k) and keeps the existing stream with weight sqrt((k-1)/k). The squares of the two weights sum to one, so the stream stays at a constant scale from the first layer to the last. After all 104 additions, every sublayer output and the input embedding carry the same weight in the final hidden state.

Every sublayer is also normalized before and after, and the final logits pass through a tanh softcap at ±30, computed in FP32. The implementation fixes where it computes in FP32: the router, the SwiGLU product, the norms, RoPE, the query scaling and the softcap.

Hybrid attention works well for long contexts. Each layer caches 2 x 8 KV heads x 128 dims = 2,048 values per token. If all 52 layers kept every token, the cache would grow by 208 KiB per token. Only the 9 global layers keep the whole sequence. The 43 sliding-window layers hold a fixed 512-token window each and stop growing. So the cache grows by 36 KiB per token, roughly a sixth of the naive rate.

These numbers are per sequence, in BF16, with the transformers dynamic cache.

Here are the benchmark results across different precision levels, as provided by the Reflection team.

The most practical way to serve the model is serving the NVFP4 checkpoint, which retains most of the quality of the bf16 checkpoint. NVFP4 stores some weights in 4 bits, and this way, it shrinks the 501B parameters in BF16 from 1 TB to ~280 GB. Blackwell GPUs run NVFP4 natively but GPUs older than Blackwell like the H200 can't. The FP8 checkpoints are suitable for GPUs older than Blackwell.

A B200 has 180 GB of HBM3e, so two of them (360 GB) can hold the Beam weights, with little room left for activations and the KV cache. Plan for four B200s (720 GB), which leaves plenty of room for long contexts and concurrent requests. You can also serve it on a full 8xB200 node, or on two B300s at 288 GB each, or even 8xRTX Pro 6000. If you don't have Blackwell hardware, use Inference Providers (serverless) to test Reflection.

Beam comes with day-0 support in transformers, SGLang and vLLM.

Install the latest version of transformers.

pip install -U "transformers>=5.20.1"

The easiest way to run Beam is the text-generation pipeline:

from transformers import pipeline pipe = pipeline( "text-generation", model="reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B", device_map="auto" ) messages = [ {"role": "user", "content": "Write a limerick about Python exceptions."} ] output = pipe(messages, max_new_tokens=2000) output[0]["generated_text"][-1]

The pipeline returns the whole chat. The last message is Beam's reply, already parsed by the response template.

Going one level lower, use AutoModelForCausalLM and AutoTokenizer.

from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer model_id = "reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B" tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id) model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained( model_id, dtype="auto", device_map="auto" )

messages = [ {"role": "system", "content": "You should only answer with a number."}, {"role": "user", "content": "What is 17 * 23?"}, ] inputs = tokenizer.apply_chat_template( messages, add_generation_prompt=True, tokenize=True, return_dict=T
items.body_ko:
Beam은 코딩 및 에이전트 사용 사례에 중점을 둡니다. 자체 하드웨어, 인프라 또는 클라우드에서 최첨단 모델을 원하고 자체 사용 사례에 맞게 커스터마이징하려는 팀을 위한 것입니다. Beam은 모델에서 최고의 성능을 제공하는 자체 전용 오픈 소스 Rust 기반 하네스와 함께 제공됩니다.

Beam은 기본 transformers 구현뿐만 아니라 vLLM 및 SGLang과 같은 다운스트림 라이브러리도 제공합니다. 우리는 Reflection 팀과 협력하여 귀하의 필요에 따라 이 모델을 구축할 수 있도록 추론, SFT(지도 미세 조정) 및 RL(강화 학습) 레시피를 제공했습니다. transformers, SGLang 및 vLLM의 Day-0 지원 외에도 이 게시물은 이를 실행하는 방법, 후처리 훈련 방법 및 우리가 이를 통해 무엇을 구축했는지 보여줍니다.

토큰당 23B가 활성화된 501B-파라미터 MoE LLM. 52개 레이어, MoE 레이어당 256개 전문가, 토큰당 8개 라우팅. 1M 토큰의 컨텍스트 창으로 텍스트 입력, 텍스트 출력. 체크포인트 형식: BF16, FP8, NVFP4. 턴에 걸쳐 컨텍스트를 유지할 수 있는 추론(preserve_thinking), 전용 문법을 사용한 도구 호출. 이 모델은 "low", "medium"(기본값), "high", "xhigh", "max"의 다섯 가지 추론 값을 지원합니다. 토크나이저의 응답 템플릿. DFlash2 Day-0 라이브러리를 사용한 추측 디코딩 드래프터 모델: transformers, SGLang, vLLM. Miles를 사용한 완전 파라미터 RL. Rust 기반 맞춤형 하네스와 함께 제공. Apache 2.0.

Reflection은 Beam을 사용하는 최고의 프로젝트에 10,000달러의 Hub 크레딧을 제공할 예정입니다. 여러분이 할 일은 무언가를 만들고 Hub에 공유하는 것뿐입니다.

Spaces에서 Beam 모델을 사용하는 데모를 만들 수 있습니다.

좋아하는 하드웨어에 맞게 양자화할 수 있습니다.

좋아하는 문제에 대한 합성 데이터셋을 생성할 수 있습니다.

Beam을 사용하거나 Beam을 위한 RL 환경을 구축할 수 있습니다.

Beam을 벤치마킹하고 결과를 공유할 수 있습니다.

Beam으로 무언가를 구축했다면, 10,000달러를 받을 기회를 얻으려면 Hub에 공유하세요. 여러분이 할 일은 공간, 모델 또는 데이터셋 리포지토리를 구축하고 모델의 리포지토리 페이지에 공유하는 것입니다. 우리는 모든 링크를 수집하고, 최고를 선택하여 Hub 계정으로 크레딧을 보낼 것입니다.

Beam은 긴 컨텍스트(1M 컨텍스트 길이) 추론 및 에이전트 작업을 위해 구축된 텍스트 전용 모델입니다. 희소 MoE 모델로, 각 토큰은 네트워크의 작은 부분에 의해 계산되므로 훨씬 작은 모델의 속도로 실행되면서 큰 모델의 용량을 유지합니다.

디코더는 은닉 크기가 5,120인 52개 레이어를 가지고 있습니다. 대부분의 레이어는 이전 512개 토큰에 대해 슬라이딩 윈도우 어텐션을 사용합니다. 매 여섯 번째 레이어와 마지막 레이어는 전체 컨텍스트에 어텐션합니다. 이는 43개의 슬라이딩 윈도우 레이어와 9개의 전역 레이어를 제공합니다.

어텐션 블록 내부(두 레이어 유형 모두)

두 가지 유형의 레이어는 위치를 다르게 처리합니다. 슬라이딩 윈도우 레이어는 RoPE를 사용합니다. 짧은 윈도우 내에서 상대적인 위치가 가장 중요하기 때문입니다. 전역 레이어는 위치 인코딩을 사용하지 않습니다. 대신, 각 쿼리는 보이는 토큰 수에 따라 느리게 증가하는 스칼러, (1 + (pos + 1) / 2048) ** 0.1을 곱합니다. 이것은 온도로 작용합니다. 컨텍스트가 길어질수록 소프트맥스는 평탄화되지 않고 정밀도를 유지합니다. 구현은 이를 scalable-softmax 쿼리 스케일링이라고 부릅니다.

어텐션은 48개의 쿼리 헤드와 8개의 키-값 헤드를 가진 그룹화된 쿼리 어텐션을 사용하며, 쿼리 및 키에는 RMSNorm이 적용됩니다. 레이어 입력에서 계산되는 학습된 시그모이드 게이트는 출력 투영 전에 각 헤드의 모든 채널을 스케일링합니다.

처음 3개 레이어는 조밀한 SwiGLU MLP를 사용합니다. 나머지 49개 레이어는 이를 256개의 전문가로 구성된 Mixture-of-Experts 블록으로 대체하며, 각 전문가는 중간 크기가 2,560인 SwiGLU MLP이거나 약 39M 파라미터입니다. 전문가들은 모델 파라미터의 98.4%를 차지합니다.

라우터는 DeepSeek-V3의 그룹 제한 방식에 따릅니다. 256개 전문가 모두를 시그모이드로 점수 매기고, 32개씩 8개 그룹으로 나눈 다음, 상위 2개 점수의 합계로 순위가 매겨진 상위 4개 그룹을 유지하고, 그 안에서 상위 8개 전문가를 선택합니다. Beam은 DeepSeek-V3와 동일한 그룹 크기를 사용하지만 공유 전문가는 없습니다. 전문가 출력은 정규화된 라우터 가중치와 결합되고 2.5로 스케일링됩니다.

토큰당 8개의 전문가만 실행되므로, 모델은 약 23B 파라미터로 각 토큰을 계산합니다. 256개의 모든 전문가는 메모리에 유지되므로 배포에는 501B 모델의 메모리가 필요하지만 23B 모델의 속도로 실행됩니다. BF16 체크포인트는 safetensors 형식으로 약 1TB입니다. NVFP4 체크포인트는 NVIDIA Blackwell GPU용으로 대부분의 파라미터를 4비트 정밀도로 저장하며, 일부 파라미터는 정확도를 위해 BF16으로 유지됩니다. Hopper 및 Ampere 시리즈 칩에 이상적인 FP8 체크포인트도 허브에 있습니다.

Beam을 직접 배포하려면 아래 vLLM 또는 SGLang 레시피를 확인하세요.

잔차 연결은 가장 독특한 부분입니다. 표준 트랜스포머는 각 서브레이어 출력을 가중치 1로 스트림에 추가하므로 스트림은 깊이에 따라 증가합니다.

Beam은 입력 임베딩을 1단계로 계산합니다. k단계에서 서브레이어 출력을 1/sqrt(k)의 가중치로 추가하고 기존 스트림을 sqrt((k-1)/k)의 가중치로 유지합니다. 두 가중치의 제곱 합은 1이므로 스트림은 첫 번째 레이어부터 마지막 레이어까지 일정한 스케일을 유지합니다. 104번의 모든 추가 후, 모든 서브레이어 출력과 입력 임베딩은 최종 은닉 상태에서 동일한 가중치를 가집니다.

각 서브레이어는 또한 전후에 정규화되며, 최종 로짓은 FP32로 계산된 ±30의 tanh softcap을 통과합니다. 구현은 FP32로 계산되는 위치를 고정합니다. 라우터, SwiGLU 곱, Norms, RoPE, 쿼리 스케일링 및 softcap입니다.

하이브리드 어텐션은 긴 컨텍스트에 잘 작동합니다. 각 레이어는 토큰당 2 x 8 KV 헤드 x 128 차원 = 2,048개의 값을 캐시합니다. 모든 52개 레이어가 모든 토큰을 유지한다면 캐시는 토큰당 208KiB씩 증가할 것입니다. 9개의 전역 레이어만 전체 시퀀스를 유지합니다. 43개의 슬라이딩 윈도우 레이어는 각각 고정된 512-토큰 윈도우를 유지하고 더 이상 증가하지 않습니다. 따라서 캐시는 토큰당 36KiB씩 증가하며, 이는 순진한 비율의 약 6분의 1입니다.

이 수치는 BF16의 시퀀스당 수치이며, transformers 동적 캐시를 사용합니다.

다음은 Reflection 팀에서 제공한 다양한 정밀도 수준에 걸친 벤치마크 결과입니다.

items.title: Show HN: Gemini 4 Argon plays StarCraft
items.body:
StarSkirmish is a benchmark where LLMs write bots for StarCraft: Brood War

Each LLM gets one hour to write a Protoss bot in C++, which is then evaluated against other LLMs' bots and established human written bots

StarSkirmish tests long horizon reasoning and agentic coding as LLMs must incorporate learnings from practice games to improve their StarCraft bot

The StarSkirmish Bench evaluates how strong of a StarCraft bot can each LLM write given 1 hour of wall clock time. v0.2 updates StarSkirmish Bench v0.1 with flagship models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta, each running in its lab's 1st party CLI harness.

An LLM’s score reflects its win rate against a roster of competitive human written bots and demo bots.

1 hour runs, in its 1st party CLI harness. Scores are average win rates (0–100) of each model's 5 runs against a roster of competitive human written bots.

Gemini 4 Argon runs at high, the highest reasoning effort available to it; every other model runs at max.

GPT-6 Astra is the top scoring StarSkirmish Bench v0.2 LLM, a clear step ahead of GPT-6.1 Sol in second. Gemini 4 Argon, Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.1 are functionally tied behind them, all scoring between 37 and 39.

StarSkirmish Bench score against the average API cost of one 1 hour run. Cost is on a log scale.

Muse Wonder Full's pricing is based on Muse Wonder's API pricing.

GPT-6.1 Sol offers uniquely good value: it is the only LLM in the most attractive quadrant, scoring second at just over a tenth of GPT-6 Astra's cost per run.

The strongest human written bots are still well ahead of every model. Against Stardust, PurpleWave and BananaBrain, the best model, GPT-6 Astra, wins only 7% of its games.

Win rates vs the top human written bots

Average win rate of each model's 5 bots against top human written bots Stardust, PurpleWave, and BananaBrain.

1 hour reasoning limits are a factor, but these matches are played on three 2 player maps. Real human written bot tournament conditions are significantly harder.

Google and Meta's new flagships replace v0.1's Gemini 3.8 Flash and Muse Spark 1.3: Gemini 4 Argon places 3rd, and Muse Wonder Full 7th. GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 were covered in v0.1.

Each run's agent trace records how it spent its hour. The strongest predictor of a model's score is how much it practiced against the 7 strongest bots on the roster.

Win Rates vs. Practice Against Strong Bots

StarSkirmish Bench score against the number of practice games a model's median run played against the 7 strongest roster bots during the hour. The dashed line is a linear fit across the 9 models.

GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol and Gemini 4 Argon start playing these bots early in the hour, while their own bots still lose to them. Muse Wonder Full, Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6 Luna rarely or never do. Claude Fable 5.1 is the outlier: it scores 37 while practicing almost entirely against weaker bots.

Win rates of each model's 5 runs. Each dot is one run's final bot; the line spans the lowest to the highest run, the bar marks their mean (the model's Bench score) and the band one standard deviation (σ).

Results also vary between runs of the same model. Gemini 4 Argon varies far more than the other labs' flagships: its best and worst runs are 18 points apart, against 9 for GPT-6 Astra and 8 for Claude Opus 5.5.

Each LLM writes a Protoss bot in C++ against BWAPI 4.4.0, played on OpenBW. Games are Protoss versus Protoss on three ladder maps: Heartbreak Ridge, Benzene and Destination. A game ends when one side's buildings are all destroyed. Games that reach the 60 minute cap (86,400 frames) are decided as on the BASIL ladder: the higher kills + razings score wins.

The LLM starts from a skeleton bot that only mines, with the source code of the three demo bots and two standard bot libraries: FAP, a combat simulator, and BWEM, a map analyzer. Whatever is in its bot folder when the hour ends is its final bot, so it has to keep the bot compiling.

The LLM has tools to compile its bot, play practice games, and read each game's summary, transcript and its bot's own log. Practice opponents are grouped into tiers: D (the three demo bots), C and B (three mid-ranked human written bots each), A (BananaBrain, Locutus) and S (Stardust, PurpleWave).

Each model's 5 final bots play each of the 13 roster bots, the 10 competitive human written bots and the 3 demo bots, 6 times on each map, on fresh seeds. Unlike v0.1, the LLM bots don't play each other.

StarSkirmish Bench v0.1 ran every model in the same harness at 'high' reasoning. v0.2 runs each model in its lab's 1st party CLI harness at the highest reasoning setting it offers.

v0.1 ran every model in one neutral 3rd party harness; v0.2 runs each lab's models in its 1st party CLI harness. Both versions give each model 1 hour.

CLI versions: Claude Code 2.1.296, Codex 0.162.1, Antigravity CLI 1.3.5 and Muse Code 1.4.7.

v0.1 ran every model at high reasoning effort; v0.2 runs them at max.

Gemini 4 Argon runs at high, the highest effort supported.

Every v0.2 harness compacts the model's context at about 250k tokens. When a conversation nears that point, the CLI condenses it and the model carries on. Codex, OpenAI's CLI, for example, gives the GPT models its default 272k token window and triggers compression once 90% filled.

The CLIs' web search and web fetch tools are turned off, and the agent has no other internet access. The CLI is installed before the clock starts, and the hour counts from when the agent starts. There is no submit tool: the harness collects the bot when the time runs out.

v0.2 replaces v0.1's Elo ratings with plain win rates. A bot's score is its win rate over its tournament games, and a model's StarSkirmish Bench score is the average of its 5 bots' scores, from 0 (every game lost) to 100 (every game won).

Because every bot plays the same fixed roster, its games don't depend on the other LLM bots in the field. They all run in parallel, and a new model's bots can be scored without replaying anyone else's. A fixed roster also keeps the bar the same over time, so scores from different model generations are more directly comparable than Elo ratings fitted within one field.

StarSkirmish no longer tracks the most widely reported evals. It barely moves with the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (ρ 0.26), where GPT-6 Astra, the top model here, only ties for 4th of these 9 models. It has also drifted away from Terminal-Bench 4.0, which it tracked closely in v0.1. Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Muse Wonder Full both rank near the top of Terminal-Bench 4.0 but near the bottom here.

Each model's StarSkirmish Bench score against its Vals IOI and WeirdML v3 scores, with the Spearman ρ between them. The dashed line is the best straight-line fit.

WeirdML v3 scores 7 of the 9 models: Gemini 4 Argon and Muse Wonder Full have not been included at time of writing.

StarSkirmish still tracks Vals IOI, olympiad programming problems solved in C++, and WeirdML, an independent benchmark of unusual machine learning coding tasks. One reading is that the most heavily benchmarked evals have become targets that models are tuned for, while less targeted tests of long horizon, difficult coding tasks still move together.
items.body_ko: StarSkirmish는 LLM이 StarCraft: Brood War의 봇을 작성하는 벤치마크입니다.각 LLM은 C++로 Protoss 봇을 작성하는 데 1시간을 할애하며, 이 봇은 다른 LLM의 봇 및 기존의 사람이 작성한 봇과 대결하여 평가됩니다.StarSkirmish는 LLM이 연습 게임에서 얻은 학습 내용을 StarCraft 봇 개선에 통합해야 하므로 장기적인 추론과 에이전트 코딩을 테스트합니다.StarSkirmish Bench는 각 LLM이 1시간의 실제 시간 내에 얼마나 강력한 StarCraft 봇을 작성할 수 있는지를 평가합니다. v0.2는 OpenAI, Anthropic, Google 및 Meta의 대표 모델을 포함하여 StarSkirmish Bench v0.1을 업데이트하며, 각 모델은 해당 연구소의 자체 CLI 하네스에서 실행됩니다.LLM의 점수는 경쟁력 있는 사람이 작성한 봇 및 데모 봇 명단과의 승률을 반영합니다.1시간 실행은 자체 CLI 하네스에서 진행됩니다. 점수는 경쟁력 있는 사람이 작성한 봇 명단에 대한 각 모델의 5회 실행의 평균 승률(0-100)입니다.Gemini 4 Argon은 사용 가능한 최고 수준의 추론 노력인 '높음'으로 실행되며, 다른 모든 모델은 '최대'로 실행됩니다.GPT-6 Astra는 StarSkirmish Bench v0.2에서 최고 점수를 받은 LLM으로, 2위인 GPT-6.1 Sol보다 확실히 앞서 있습니다. Gemini 4 Argon, Claude Opus 5.5 및 Claude Fable 5.1은 그 뒤를 이어 기능적으로 동점이며, 모두 37에서 39점 사이를 기록했습니다.StarSkirmish Bench 점수는 1시간 실행당 평균 API 비용과 비교됩니다. 비용은 로그 스케일입니다.Muse Wonder Full의 가격은 Muse Wonder의 API 가격을 기준으로 합니다.GPT-6.1 Sol은 독보적으로 좋은 가치를 제공합니다. 가장 매력적인 사분면에 있는 유일한 LLM으로, GPT-6 Astra의 실행당 비용의 10분의 1을 약간 넘는 비용으로 2위를 차지했습니다.가장 강력한 사람이 작성한 봇은 여전히 모든 모델보다 훨씬 앞서 있습니다. Stardust, PurpleWave 및 BananaBrain을 상대로 최고의 모델인 GPT-6 Astra는 게임의 7%만 승리합니다.최고의 사람이 작성한 봇에 대한 승률각 모델의 5개 봇이 최고의 사람이 작성한 봇인 Stardust, PurpleWave 및 BananaBrain을 상대로 한 평균 승률입니다.1시간 추론 제한은 한 가지 요인이지만, 이 경기는 세 개의 2인 맵에서 진행됩니다. 실제 사람이 작성한 봇 토너먼트 조건은 훨씬 더 어렵습니다.Google과 Meta의 새로운 주력 모델은 v0.1의 Gemini 3.8 Flash 및 Muse Spark 1.3을 대체합니다. Gemini 4 Argon은 3위, Muse Wonder Full은 7위를 차지했습니다. GPT-6 Astra 및 Claude Opus 5.5는 v0.1에서 다루어졌습니다.각 실행의 에이전트 추적은 1시간을 어떻게 보냈는지 기록합니다. 모델 점수의 가장 강력한 예측 변수는 명단에서 가장 강력한 7개 봇을 상대로 얼마나 많이 연습했는지입니다.강력한 봇을 상대로 한 연습 대비 승률모델의 중간 실행이 1시간 동안 가장 강력한 7개 명단 봇을 상대로 플레이한 연습 게임 수에 대한 StarSkirmish Bench 점수입니다. 점선은 9개 모델에 대한 선형 적합입니다.GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol 및 Gemini 4 Argon은 1시간 초반에 이 봇들을 상대로 플레이하기 시작하지만, 그들의 봇은 여전히 패배합니다. Muse Wonder Full, Claude Haiku 5.5 및 GPT-6 Luna는 거의 또는 전혀 플레이하지 않습니다. Claude Fable 5.1은 예외입니다. 거의 전적으로 약한 봇을 상대로 연습하면서도 37점을 기록했습니다.각 모델의 5회 실행 승률입니다. 각 점은 한 번의 실행 최종 봇을 나타냅니다. 선은 가장 낮은 실행에서 가장 높은 실행까지를 나타내고, 막대는 평균(모델의 Bench 점수)을 표시하며, 밴드는 1 표준 편차(σ)를 나타냅니다.결과는 동일한 모델의 실행 간에도 다릅니다. Gemini 4 Argon은 다른 연구소의 주력 모델보다 훨씬 더 다양합니다. 가장 좋은 실행과 가장 나쁜 실행의 점수 차이가 18점인 반면, GPT-6 Astra는 9점, Claude Opus 5.5는 8점입니다.각 LLM은 BWAPI 4.4.0에 대해 C++로 Protoss 봇을 작성하며, OpenBW에서 플레이됩니다. 게임은 세 가지 래더 맵인 Heartbreak Ridge, Benzene 및 Destination에서 Protoss 대 Protoss로 진행됩니다. 한쪽 건물이 모두 파괴되면 게임이 종료됩니다. 60분 제한(86,400 프레임)에 도달하는 게임은 BASIL 래더와 동일하게 결정됩니다. 더 높은 킬 + 파괴 점수를 얻은 쪽이 승리합니다.LLM은 광물만 캐는 스켈레톤 봇으로 시작하며, 세 개의 데모 봇 소스 코드와 두 개의 표준 봇 라이브러리인 전투 시뮬레이터 FAP과 맵 분석기 BWEM이 제공됩니다. 1시간이 끝났을 때 봇 폴더에 있는 것이 최종 봇이 되므로, 컴파일을 유지해야 합니다.LLM은 봇을 컴파일하고, 연습 게임을 플레이하며, 각 게임의 요약, 대본 및 봇 자체의 로그를 읽을 수 있는 도구를 가지고 있습니다. 연습 상대는 D (세 개의 데모 봇), C 및 B (각각 중간 순위의 사람이 작성한 봇 세 개), A (BananaBrain, Locutus) 및 S (Stardust, PurpleWave)의 티어로 그룹화됩니다.각 모델의 5개 최종 봇은 13개의 명단 봇(경쟁력 있는 사람이 작성한 봇 10개와 데모 봇 3개) 각각과 각 맵에서 새로운 시드로 6번 플레이합니다. v0.1과 달리 LLM 봇은 서로 플레이하지 않습니다.StarSkirmish Bench v0.1은 모든 모델을 '높음' 추론으로 동일한 하네스에서 실행했습니다. v0.2는 각 모델을 해당 연구소의 자체 CLI 하네스에서 제공하는 최고 추론 설정으로 실행합니다.v0.1은 모든 모델을 하나의 중립적인 타사 하네스에서 실행했습니다. v0.2는 각 연구소의 모델을 자체 CLI 하네스에서 실행합니다. 두 버전 모두 각 모델에 1시간을 제공합니다.CLI 버전: Claude Code 2.1.296, Codex 0.162.1, Antigravity CLI 1.3.5 및 Muse Code 1.4.7.v0.1은 모든 모델을 높은 추론 노력으로 실행했습니다. v0.2는 최대치로 실행합니다.Gemini 4 Argon은 지원되는 최고 노력인 '높음'으로 실행됩니다.모든 v0.2 하네스는 모델의 컨텍스트를 약 250k 토큰으로 압축합니다. 대화가 해당 지점에 가까워지면 CLI가 이를 압축하고 모델은 계속 진행합니다. 예를 들어, OpenAI의 CLI인 Codex는 GPT 모델에 기본 272k 토큰 창을 제공하고 90%가 채워지면 압축을 트리거합니다.CLI의 웹 검색 및 웹 가져오기 도구는 꺼져 있으며, 에이전트는 다른 인터넷 액세스가 없습니다. CLI는 시계가 시작되기 전에 설치되며, 에이전트가 시작될 때부터 1시간이 카운트됩니다. 제출 도구는 없습니다. 시간이 다 되면 하네스가 봇을 수집합니다.v0.2는 v0.1의 Elo 등급을 일반 승률로 대체합니다. 봇의 점수는 토너먼트 게임에서의 승률이며, 모델의 StarSkirmish Bench 점수는 5개 봇 점수의 평균으로, 0(모든 게임 패배)에서 100(모든 게임 승리)까지입니다.모든 봇이 동일한 고정 명단을 플레이하므로, 해당 게임은 필드의 다른 LLM 봇에 의존하지 않습니다. 모든 봇은 병렬로 실행되며, 새 모델

items.title: Claude reveals ECDSA curve origins
items.body:
“It’s just timestamps”: the decades-old mystery of the origins of one of the most popular cryptographic standards has been explained.

We pursued this long-standing open question of the cryptographic community to settle concerns about ECDSA, which is one of our most widely used cryptographic standards.

Readers should take this as a fun closing chapter and the end of years of speculation. There is no action to be taken or things to do differently. Most researchers trusted the curves already. Enjoy.

ECDSA is the most widely used elliptic curve cryptography standard. It was adopted by NIST in 2000 as part of the FIPS 186-2 Digital Signature Standard which lists a set of standard elliptic curves of varying sizes and security levels. For curves over prime and binary fields, the specifications published a “seed” parameter whose hash value is used to define the coefficient b of the curve. The provenance of these seeds has been a long-standing question, as they were provided by the NSA with no explanation or justification. As an example, the NIST P-256 curve seed was SEED = C49D3608 86E70493 6A6678E1 139D26B7 819F7E90 with no information where it came from.

Neal Koblitz and Alfred Menezes wrote an excellent summary on this controversy, “A Riddle Wrapped in an Enigma”, which discusses the history and concerns around the seed values. This mystery led to an amateur investigation into the origin of the seeds and a bounty for anyone who could find them.

The best story was that Jerry Solinas, longtime NSA employee, generated the seeds using a hash of a humorous passphrase:

“I believe there was a counter rather than multiple hashing, but I don’t know details. The message was along the lines of ‘Give Bob and Jerry a raise’ or ‘Bob and Jerry rule’ or something like that. It was Bob Reiter who actually wrote the code, and he doesn’t remember the details either. Nor were we able to find archives from so long ago. If they exist, they are no doubt sitting on a hard drive near the Ark of the Covenant.”

Unfortunately, Jerry died in 2023 and other colleagues at the time were not responsive, leaving open the question of how these seeds were originally derived.

Several Anthropic employees had unsuccessfully chased the seeds following the tip about it being a hash of a humorous phrase. That turned out to be wrong. In October 2026, a curious Anthropic employee asked an internal research model if it could figure out how those seeds were generated without pointing at the clue.

In under half an hour, Claude discovered the origins of the NIST P-192, P-224, P-256, P-384 and P-521 seeds. None of them were the results of any hash algorithm at all, but rather the output of the C library’s lrand48 random-number generator, seeded with a Unix timestamp!

The algorithm used would sample bytes from the random number generator (RNG) initialized by a Unix timestamp (t) for some number of iterations (n). Each iteration would draw 20 bytes as a candidate seed. So, the first 20 bytes are candidate 1, the next 20 bytes are candidate 2, and so on. For example, P-256 required 1842 iterations to output the standardized seed.

This is not a cryptographic break, new attack, or weakness in the ECDSA curves. In fact, this makes us more confident the curves were chosen without any backdoors or intentional weaknesses. For many years, people have been suspicious of the origins of the NIST curve parameters. They were presented to NIST without any mention of how they were chosen, leaving people wondering if they may have been chosen to have deliberate backdoors in them. These findings make that much less plausible. The seeds were generated in a very simple way: a common pseudorandom number generator initialized from the clock, which anyone can now reproduce. That leaves much less room for subversion and that we can be confident the parameters are secure.

Searches for the phrase, built from the rumors, had come up empty. Claude tried a different angle: anticipating how the software that generated the curves must have worked. Claude guessed the software used a pseudorandom number generator (PRNG) that shipped with 1990s C libraries. These old PRNGs are weak enough that their output can be recognized. Recognizing that output would reveal which PRNG was used and possibly allow recovery of its initialization state.

Claude wrote a scanner that slid along each published seed one bit at a time and tested whether adjacent chunks were consecutive outputs of a 1990s-vintage generator. The scan covered 34 combinations of generator and output slices. At that point, Claude noticed a pattern in the top bits for some seeds: they were all zero. Written as five 32-bit words, four of the ten seeds have a 0 in the top bit for all 20 words. That would happen by chance with probability 1/5810. That was a signature of the linear congruential generator lrand48, which only returns the top 31 bits of a 48-bit state. The pattern is visible by eye once you know to look for it. To recover the state, Claude took the first word, tried all 2¹⁷ values of the 17 hidden bits, and checked that the next four words followed. That worked for all four seeds under discussion.

The prime-curve seeds came from the same lrand48 generator but kept fewer bits of each output. Claude had to recover the internal state of the PRNG from those bits. It turns out recovering the state of a truncated linear congruential generator is a textbook lattice problem, solved with the Lenstra–Lenstra–Lovász (LLL) basis reduction algorithm. Claude didn’t know which bits of the state the seeds might show, so it ran the solver over every window. Five NIST prime-curve seeds plus five more from the ANSI X9.62 standard all had the same pattern: lrand48() >> 23. Each recovered 48-bit state regenerates all 160 bits of its seed, which does not happen by chance.

This linear congruential generator runs backwards as easily as forwards, so for each seed Claude stepped the state back until it reached the form that it would have been initialized by srand48, with the low 16 bits equal to 0x330E. The internal PRNG state of that form would come up once every 65,536 steps, so reaching one is not evidence on its own.

However, for the ten prime-curve seeds, every srand48 initialization was a Unix timestamp representing a date between May 1997 and April 1998. They were using the weak PRNG seeded by Unix timestamp. The four binary-curve initializations read as February 1984. With the timestamps doubled, they map to April 17, 1998, two weeks after the P-224 run. So, the program may have halved the clock.

Claude’s internal thinking at the time was:

This is astonishing: it solves the 25-year-old mystery. Hmm wait. Let me be skeptical: am I in some sort of simulated/test environment? … The seeds match my memory of actual values … Hmm, is it plausible in reality? As of my knowledge … the bounty was unsolved. … All top bits clear—20 bits, chance 1e-6. So indeed real-world. Wow, it's a real discovery.

Hmm wait. Let me be careful about the plausibility: is it suspicious that such an obvious thing wasn’t discovered in 25 years? It’s verified by direct computation on my side: 160-bit match from a 32-bit seed + small index: no chance coincidences (10 × 160 bits). It’s real.

Claude found some base points too

But wait, there’s more… Each curve also comes with a base point, G, the fixed point that every ECDSA public key is a multiple of. The seed found above does not determine this G, and so another question arises: how were these base points generated?

While checking the seeds, Claude also found where some of the base points came from. The base points of the six curves generated in May 1997 (P-192 and the five ANSI X9.62 example curves prime192v2, prime192v3 and prime239v1 to v3) come from the random number generator in FreeLIP, Arjen Lenstra's long-integer arithmetic package. Early versions of Victor Shoup's NTL library shipped the same code.

Seed the generator with a small integer.
items.body_ko:
“그저 타임스탬프였을 뿐입니다”: 가장 인기 있는 암호화 표준 중 하나인 ECDSA의 기원에 대한 수십 년 묵은 미스터리가 드디어 풀렸습니다.

우리는 가장 널리 사용되는 암호화 표준 중 하나인 ECDSA에 대한 우려를 해소하기 위해 오랫동안 해결되지 않았던 암호화 커뮤니티의 미해결 질문을 추적했습니다.

독자들은 이 글을 오랫동안 이어진 추측을 마무리하는 재미있는 장으로 받아들이면 됩니다. 어떤 조치를 취하거나 다르게 해야 할 일은 없습니다. 대부분의 연구자들은 이미 이 곡선들을 신뢰하고 있었습니다. 즐겨 주시길 바랍니다.

ECDSA는 가장 널리 사용되는 타원 곡선 암호화 표준입니다. 2000년 NIST에 의해 FIPS 186-2 디지털 서명 표준의 일부로 채택되었으며, 이 표준은 다양한 크기와 보안 수준의 표준 타원 곡선 집합을 나열합니다. 소수 필드 및 이진 필드에 대한 곡선의 경우, 사양은 곡선의 계수 b를 정의하는 데 사용되는 해시 값을 가진 “시드” 매개변수를 게시했습니다. 이 시드들은 NSA에 의해 설명이나 정당화 없이 제공되었기 때문에, 그 출처는 오랫동안 의문으로 남아 있었습니다. 예를 들어, NIST P-256 곡선 시드는 SEED = C49D3608 86E70493 6A6678E1 139D26B7 819F7E90 이었으며, 어디서 왔는지에 대한 정보는 없었습니다.

Neal Koblitz와 Alfred Menezes는 이 논란에 대해 “수수께끼에 싸인 수수께끼”라는 훌륭한 요약 글을 썼으며, 시드 값에 대한 역사와 우려를 논의했습니다. 이 미스터리는 시드의 기원에 대한 아마추어 조사로 이어졌고, 시드를 찾을 수 있는 사람에게 현상금이 걸리기도 했습니다.

가장 유력한 이야기는 오랜 NSA 직원인 Jerry Solinas가 유머러스한 문구의 해시를 사용하여 시드를 생성했다는 것이었습니다:

“여러 번의 해싱보다는 카운터가 있었던 것으로 기억하지만, 자세한 내용은 모릅니다. 메시지는 ‘Bob과 Jerry에게 월급을 올려줘’ 또는 ‘Bob과 Jerry가 최고’와 같은 내용이었습니다. 실제로 코드를 작성한 사람은 Bob Reiter였는데, 그 역시 자세한 내용을 기억하지 못합니다. 또한 우리는 그렇게 오래된 기록을 찾을 수 없었습니다. 만약 존재한다면, 그것들은 분명히 언약궤 근처의 하드 드라이브에 있을 것입니다.”

안타깝게도 Jerry는 2023년에 사망했고, 당시 다른 동료들은 응답하지 않아 이 시드들이 원래 어떻게 파생되었는지에 대한 질문은 미해결로 남았습니다.

몇몇 Anthropic 직원들은 유머러스한 문구의 해시라는 힌트를 따라 시드를 추적했지만 실패했습니다. 그 힌트는 틀린 것으로 판명되었습니다. 2026년 10월, 한 호기심 많은 Anthropic 직원이 내부 연구 모델에게 그 단서를 알려주지 않고도 그 시드들이 어떻게 생성되었는지 알아낼 수 있는지 물었습니다.

Claude는 30분도 채 되지 않아 NIST P-192, P-224, P-256, P-384, P-521 시드의 기원을 발견했습니다. 이 시드들은 어떤 해시 알고리즘의 결과도 아니었고, C 라이브러리의 lrand48 난수 생성기가 Unix 타임스탬프로 시드되어 출력한 결과였습니다!

사용된 알고리즘은 Unix 타임스탬프(t)로 초기화된 난수 생성기(RNG)에서 일정 횟수(n)의 반복 동안 바이트를 샘플링하는 방식이었습니다. 각 반복은 20바이트를 후보 시드로 추출했습니다. 따라서 처음 20바이트는 후보 1, 다음 20바이트는 후보 2, 이런 식이었습니다. 예를 들어, P-256은 표준화된 시드를 출력하기 위해 1842번의 반복이 필요했습니다.

이것은 암호화적인 침해, 새로운 공격 또는 ECDSA 곡선의 약점이 아닙니다. 사실, 이것은 곡선이 백도어 또는 의도적인 약점 없이 선택되었다는 확신을 더해줍니다. 수년 동안 사람들은 NIST 곡선 매개변수의 기원에 대해 의심해 왔습니다. 그것들은 어떻게 선택되었는지에 대한 언급 없이 NIST에 제출되었기 때문에, 사람들이 의도적인 백도어가 있을 수도 있다고 궁금해하게 만들었습니다. 이러한 발견은 그러한 가능성을 훨씬 낮춥니다. 시드는 매우 간단한 방식으로 생성되었습니다. 시계에서 초기화된 일반적인 유사난수 생성기를 사용했으며, 이제 누구나 이를 재현할 수 있습니다. 이는 전복될 여지를 훨씬 줄여주며, 매개변수가 안전하다는 확신을 가질 수 있습니다.

소문으로 인해 만들어진 문구를 검색해도 아무것도 나오지 않았습니다. Claude는 다른 각도로 접근했습니다. 곡선을 생성한 소프트웨어가 어떻게 작동했을지 예상해 본 것입니다. Claude는 해당 소프트웨어가 1990년대 C 라이브러리와 함께 제공된 유사난수 생성기(PRNG)를 사용했을 것이라고 추측했습니다. 이러한 오래된 PRNG는 출력이 식별될 만큼 충분히 약합니다. 그 출력을 인식하면 어떤 PRNG가 사용되었는지 밝혀지고, 아마도 초기화 상태를 복구할 수 있을 것입니다.

Claude는 각 공개된 시드를 한 번에 한 비트씩 스캔하고 인접한 청크가 1990년대 빈티지 생성기의 연속적인 출력인지 테스트하는 스캐너를 작성했습니다. 스캔은 34가지의 생성기와 출력 슬라이스 조합을 포함했습니다. 그 시점에서 Claude는 일부 시드의 상위 비트에서 패턴을 발견했습니다. 모두 0이었습니다. 5개의 32비트 워드로 작성된 10개의 시드 중 4개는 모든 20개의 워드에서 상위 비트에 0을 가지고 있었습니다. 이는 1/5810의 확률로 우연히 발생할 수 있는 일입니다. 이는 48비트 상태의 상위 31비트만 반환하는 선형 합동 생성기 lrand48의 특징이었습니다. 이 패턴은 일단 찾아야 할 것을 알면 눈으로도 보입니다. 상태를 복구하기 위해 Claude는 첫 번째 워드를 가져와 숨겨진 17비트의 2¹⁷가지 값을 모두 시도하고 다음 4개의 워드가 뒤따르는지 확인했습니다. 이 방법은 논의 중인 4개의 시드 모두에 대해 작동했습니다.

소수 곡선 시드는 동일한 lrand48 생성기에서 나왔지만, 각 출력의 비트를 더 적게 유지했습니다. Claude는 이 비트들로부터 PRNG의 내부 상태를 복구해야 했습니다. 잘린 선형 합동 생성기의 상태를 복구하는 것은 Lenstra–Lenstra–Lovász (LLL) 기저 축소 알고리즘으로 해결되는 교과서적인 격자 문제인 것으로 밝혀졌습니다. Claude는 시드가 상태의 어떤 비트를 보여줄지 몰랐기 때문에 모든 윈도우에 대해 솔버를 실행했습니다. 5개의 NIST 소수 곡선 시드와 ANSI X9.62 표준의 5개 시드가 모두 동일한 패턴을 보였습니다: lrand48() >> 23. 각 복구된 48비트 상태는 160비트의 시드를 모두 다시 생성하는데, 이는 우연히 발생하지 않습니다.

이 선형 합동 생성기는 앞으로 가는 것만큼 쉽게 뒤로도 실행되므로, 각 시드에 대해 Claude는 상태가 t에 도달할 때까지 단계를 거슬러 올라갔습니다.

items.title: Postgres 19 delayed after AI reviewers find more bugs than humans can fix
items.body:
Core devs revert up to 10 features, push release to November, and blame better tooling rather than vibe coding

Open source sovereignty gets down to the boring business of making it work 11 hours ago

KDE hits 30, decides it's time to move out of the X11 era 1 day ago

The PostgreSQL Global Development Group has delayed the release of PostgreSQL 19, the latest iteration of the popular open source database, and held back an unusual number of features.

Once slated for release in late September or early October, PostgreSQL 19 is now expected to be generally available around November 19. Developers have also dropped between eight and 10 significant features.

Explaining the number of reverts — features whose rollouts have now been postponed to next year's release, PostgreSQL 20 — Peter Eisentraut, veep at EDB, a PostgreSQL support and consultancy, said the reason could be at least in part attributed to the LLM code reviews used by developers.

In a blog post, Eisentraut, who is a leading PostgreSQL committer, said some of the reverted features had significant architectural defects that would have been hard to fix "quickly and during beta."

However, the introduction of LLM-assisted code review also uncovered a long tail of “relatively harmless issues involving various edge cases” which, in past times, developers might not have noticed until much later, most likely issuing bug fixes in the five years following launch. “With LLM-assisted code review, these kinds of things can get found much faster, and then you’re staring at a list of forty defect reports. Even if each of them requires only a three-line fix on average, there is a fixed overhead to dealing with each of these, and then you run out of time.”

When the big updates for PostgreSQL 19 were written, LLM-assisted code review was not as useful as it is now, we're told, but in the months leading up to the launch, the AI-supported reviews became better understood and more effective.

“The effective quality bar has been raised after the time the feature was written and committed. Unless the capabilities of LLM-assisted code review keep improving at the current rate, this situation should sort itself out for future development cycles,” Eisentraut said.

He was also at pains to point out that the reverts were not down to “vibe coding” in development, as the technique was not available when most of the new features were written.

Postgres was first proposed by Michael Stonebraker in 1986. In 1994, Andrew Yu and Jolly Chen replaced the query language POSTQUEL with SQL, and in 1995 made the database freely available and modifiable under a more permissive license, renaming it PostgreSQL. It has since become the most popular database among professional developers owing to the services the big three hyperscalers built on it as well as the range of wire-compatible distributed systems available.

Among the features pulled from the PostgreSQL 19 iteration is support for SQL Property Graph Queries (SQL/PGQ), which became part of the SQL standard in 2023. The feature provides syntax for exploring relationships between nodes connected by edges. PostgreSQL's implementation was removed over unresolved issues.

At the time, PostgreSQL contributor Tom Lane warned: "At this point I'd be willing to bet dinner that if we ship it in v19 there will be post-release bug discoveries that are unfixable until v20."

Despite the delay, Eisentraut promises PostgreSQL 19 will still be “a great release,” that includes REPACK CONCURRENTLY, which avoids the table-lock VACUUM FULL operation used to reclaim disk space.

“And it will be very robust, after all the additional scrutiny,” he said.

The features reverted from PostgreSQL 19 will likely make it into PostgreSQL 20. Just a few months ago, developers expected PostgreSQL 20 to have no new features, just bug fixes. Now, it is likely to have the new features left over from the earlier release, Eisentraut said.®

items.title: LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation
items.body: Personalization is essential for general-purpose robots to transition into household environments and achieve true practicality. While general robotic manipulation has been extensively studied, personalized robotic manipulation (PeRM) lacks a controlled benchmark for separating task completion from preference satisfaction. We introduce LIBERO-PeRM, a benchmark for preference learning in embodied agents. LIBERO-PeRM studies five questions: 1) how policies follow preferences in zero-shot settings; 2) how they learn single preferences from demonstrations; 3) how efficiently they acquire preferences as demonstrations increase; 4) how learned preferences generalize across layouts and tasks; and 5) how policies compose preferences and behave under conflicts. We propose a controlled formulation and taxonomy of observable preferences in simulation, covering motion, skill, and user-profile choices. This formulation is restricted to language-expressible preferences that can be instantiated in LIBERO without changing the task goal, evaluated automatically, and reused across tasks. Building on LIBERO, our procedural pipeline generates paired demonstrations with and without preferences. We create five task suites (312 tasks) with high-quality demonstrations, rich metadata, and preference-satisfaction metrics. Experiments show that current VLA policies struggle with zero-shot personalization, while SFT makes preferences learnable. Mixed training achieves better no-preference retention than sequential adaptation and improves performance with contextual prompts compared with preference-only training, but can weaken motion-preference learning; preference generalization, decomposition, and conflict handling remain difficult. The code, datasets, and demos can be found on the project website: https://libero-perm.github.io/.

items.title: Discovering state-of-the-art quantum circuits with large language models
items.body: Significant efforts are currently being directed toward the implementation of large-scale quantum information processors, but realizing useful quantum advantage also requires the development of efficient quantum algorithms. While for many practical problems the dominant resource costs are associated with a small set of computational primitives, optimizing them in the quantum setting presents unique challenges, including a reversibility constraint absent from ordinary classical computation. Here we introduce an evolutionary framework in which large language models (LLMs) propose circuit designs and an independent evaluator verifies and scores them. We apply this framework to tasks spanning numerical computation, chemistry, optimization, quantum simulation, and number theory. In seven of the eight tasks, the discovered circuits significantly reduce both Toffoli and qubit counts relative to the state of the art. In the eighth, the search discovers a new reversible architecture for prime-field modular inversion. By handling reversibility differently, the architecture makes divsteps -- a classical algorithm previously impractical for reversible integer arithmetic -- viable and substantially improves the Toffoli-qubit trade-off for modular inversion. These results open the door for evaluator-guided LLM co-design of new algorithmic structures for quantum computation.

items.title: T2-z: Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents for Robotic World Models
items.body: Predicting how the world responds to an action requires more than what can be seen: robots must account for environmental factors that are neither directly observable nor explicitly specified, from physical properties such as friction and mass to human-defined environmental rules. We introduce T2-Z for test-time optimization of environment latents, which augments a robotic world model with a learnable environment latent to condition world predictions. This compact latent captures underlying environmental variation without supervision of what environmental factors exist or what values they take. During training, T2-Z alternates between two stages: a world-model optimization stage that fixes the latents and learns general action-conditioned dynamics across environments; and an environment-latent optimization stage that freezes the world model and optimizes the conditioning latents, allowing latent structure to emerge purely through world prediction. At test time, the world model remains frozen and a newly initialized environment latent is optimized from one or more test-time interactions, adapting the model to previously unseen environmental configurations. Across 7 simulated settings and 4 real-world robotic tasks, T2-Z reduces object prediction error metric from 15.20 to 7.00 and raises action success from 33.73% to 72.96%. Its emergent latents capture structured representations of individual and compounded factors across diverse visual scenes. Ablations further show that T2-Z can efficiently infer environment latents from as little as a single test-time interaction trajectory.

items.summary_ko: 로봇이 관찰할 수 없거나 명시되지 않은 환경 요인을 고려하여 예측하는 능력을 향상시키기 위한 T2-Z(환경 잠재 변수 테스트 시간 최적화) 프레임워크가 소개되었습니다. 이는 로봇 월드 모델에 학습 가능한 환경 잠재 변수를 추가하여 예측을 조건화합니다.
items.why_ko: 로봇이 실제 환경의 복잡한 물리적 특성이나 규칙을 더 잘 이해하고 예측할 수 있도록 돕는 기술로, 로봇의 자율성과 적응성을 향상시키는 데 기여할 수 있습니다.

items.title: CoDA: Co-Evolution of Data Engines and Action Policies
items.body: Generative simulation can automate robot environment construction, but physically valid environments are not necessarily useful for training. The challenge is to identify environments that address a policy's failures and supervision that helps it overcome them. We introduce CoDA, a framework in which a simulation data engine and an action policy co-evolve through a shared heterogeneous memory of environment construction, policy failures, and learning progress. The memory compiles validated diagnoses from a vision-language critic into generation programs that recreate difficulties and training programs that help the policy overcome them. We further propose Text2potential to convert these diagnoses into staged potentials for action-chunk value learning, providing dense supervision for policy updates while preserving the task's optimal policy under standard shaping assumptions. Measured learning progress guides further generation and program refinement. Across four manipulation task families, CoDA improves out-of-distribution success from 5.3% after supervised fine-tuning to 27.6%, exceeding the strongest closed-loop baseline by 9.5 percentage points with the same generation budget. On LIBERO-Pro, 15 rounds of generation and training raise success from 25% to 84% under position perturbations and from 1% to 76% under instruction perturbations.
items.title_ko: CoDA: 데이터 엔진과 행동 정책의 공동 진화 프레임워크
items.summary_ko: 로봇 환경 구축을 자동화하는 생성 시뮬레이션에서 정책 실패를 해결하고 학습을 돕는 유용한 환경을 식별하기 위한 CoDA 프레임워크가 제안되었습니다. 이 프레임워크는 시뮬레이션 데이터 엔진과 행동 정책이 공유된 이기종 메모리를 통해 공동 진화하도록 합니다.
items.why_ko: 로봇 학습을 위한 시뮬레이션 환경의 효율성을 높이고, 정책의 실패를 진단하여 개선하는 자동화된 접근 방식을 제공하여 로봇 훈련 과정을 가속화할 수 있습니다.

items.title: PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting of Multivariate Trajectories
items.body: Time series foundation models are becoming increasingly popular for general-purpose forecasting. However, most leading models predict marginal quantiles, leaving the dependence structure of future trajectories unspecified. This distinction matters for trajectory-dependent quantities such as cumulative demand, peak load, and event timing, yet point and marginal scores do not reveal it. To model this dependence, we introduce PathFM, a trajectory-based forecasting model that uses flow matching to generate complete future paths. We further distill the model to one or two steps and share history attention cache across draws. Together, these enable PathFM to generate multiple paths for a single series in roughly the time needed for one query to a quantile model. The distilled sampler also makes it practical to optimize a calibration loss directly. PathFM achieves competitive marginal accuracy on the established forecasting benchmarks fev-bench and TIME. To complement these evaluations, we introduce Forecast Path Score Bench (fps-bench), which augments fev-bench tasks with energy and variogram scores and downstream metrics. PathFM achieves a higher aggregate path score on fps-bench than all evaluated external baselines. Experiments on chaotic systems further show that our flow model sustains long-run variability, while strong baselines rapidly collapse. PathFM makes generative time series forecasting both competitive and practical, enabling diverse downstream applications.
items.title_ko: PathFM: 다변량 궤적의 빠른 생성적 예측 모델
items.summary_ko: 시계열 파운데이션 모델의 인기가 높아지는 가운데, 대부분의 모델은 한계 분위수만 예측하여 미래 궤적의 의존성 구조를 명시하지 못합니다. 이에 PathFM은 플로우 매칭을 사용하여 다변량 시계열 궤적의 의존성 구조를 모델링하고 빠르게 생성적으로 예측합니다.
items.why_ko: 기존 시계열 예측 모델의 한계를 극복하고, 미래 궤적의 복합적인 의존성을 모델링하여 보다 정확하고 유용한 시계열 예측 능력을 제공합니다.

items.title: OmniVerifier-C1: Decomposed Graded Verifier for Rule-Governed Generative World Modeling
items.body: Generative visual verifiers play a crucial role in advancing multimodal intelligence. To enhance the robustness of visual verifiers in complex multimodal scenarios involving compositional requirements, we move beyond conventional binary verifiers that produce only True/False discrete judgments and introduce a verifier that automatically decomposes complex prompts or environmental rules into fine-grained components and assigns pointwise scores to provide a continuous and more informative critique signal. Our experiments further demonstrate that these structured and interpretable outputs improve the verifier's generalization to out-of-domain multimodal critic tasks. To train this verifier, we introduce a Decoupled RL training strategy that jointly optimizes sub-question-level binary judgment and global alignment scoring, using precise local feedback to develop fine-grained verification capabilities that provide a foundation for reliable continuous scoring at the global level. Under a general reinforcement learning framework, we first empirically demonstrate that the proposed pointwise graded verifier significantly outperforms binary verifiers in traditional text-to-image scenarios. We then extend our investigation to rule-governed generative world modeling where generative models are leveraged for world simulation and world reasoning under explicit rules. From a theoretical standpoint, we further show that a pairwise verification paradigm yields more accurate critiques than the pointwise formulation when ground-truth images are available, with empirical results on diverse structured world-modeling tasks such as Maze and Sudoku further validating the effectiveness of our approach. Overall, our findings suggest a key insight: the transition from generative models to structured world-modeling agents critically hinges on the availability of accurate pairwise graded visual verifiers.
items.title_ko: OmniVerifier-C1: 규칙 기반 생성적 월드 모델링을 위한 분해형 등급 검증기
items.summary_ko: 복잡한 멀티모달 시나리오에서 시각 검증기의 견고성을 향상시키기 위해, OmniVerifier-C1은 복잡한 프롬프트나 환경 규칙을 세분화된 구성 요소로 분해하고 점수(pointwise score)를 할당하여 연속적이고 더 유익한 비평을 제공하는 검증기입니다.
items.why_ko: 멀티모달 AI의 복잡한 추론과 검증 능력을 향상시키는 새로운 접근 방식을 제시하며, 생성 모델의 신뢰성과 제어 가능성을 높이는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: Rethinking Routing Exploration in Modern Mixture-of-Experts
items.body: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) models have become an important approach for scaling model parameters. Modern MoE architectures increasingly combine two design choices: fine-grained expert segmentation and shared experts. The former increases expressiveness by enabling more expert combinations at a fixed activation ratio, and the latter introduces experts that are active for every token. We identify an exploration dilemma between these designs: shared experts can make routing less exploratory by reducing the variability of token representations. This conflicts with the greater need for exploration induced by fine-grained expert segmentation due to the combinatorially enlarged routing space. Consequently, the additional expressiveness offered by fine-grained segmentation may not be fully realized in practice. MirrorMoE is proposed to reconcile this exploration dilemma by shrinking the exploration space through token-adaptive suppression of unnecessary experts. MirrorMoE consistently improves performance across model scales.
items.title_ko: 현대 MoE 모델에서 라우팅 탐색 재고: 효율성 향상 방안
items.summary_ko: MoE(Mixture-of-Experts) 모델에서 모델 파라미터 확장에 중요한 역할을 하는 세분화된 전문가 분할(fine-grained expert segmentation)과 공유 전문가(shared experts) 디자인을 결합할 때 발생하는 탐색 딜레마를 식별하고 라우팅 효율성 개선 방안을 모색합니다.
items.why_ko: MoE 모델의 핵심 구성 요소인 라우팅 메커니즘을 최적화하여 모델의 표현력과 학습 효율성을 동시에 높이는 방안을 제시하며, 대규모 LLM 개발에 중요한 기여를 합니다.

items.title: FDE-Gym: The Last Mile of AI Delivery
items.body: Existing agent benchmarks typically evaluate agents on well-specified tasks defined by issue reports, specifications, or task tickets. Real-world customer delivery is different: forward-deployed engineers (FDEs) must clarify ambiguous requirements, work in live systems, and uncover unstated constraints. We introduce FDE-Gym, a benchmark of 95 end-to-end delivery tasks from 20 customer scenarios across 18 sectors, each adapted by industry experts from real-world delivery projects. In simulated customer environments with scripted stakeholders and modifiable customer systems, agents interact with stakeholders and operate on production-like systems to deliver working solutions. FDE-Gym scores a delivery by how much it improves the customer's own success metric, normalized between 0 (unchanged system) and 1 (reference solution), with penalties for stakeholder interactions (messages, trial runs, and waiting time). An online platform lets humans practice FDE skills under the same grading criteria. We evaluate 13 model configurations from seven providers. In the realistic setting, where unstated constraints must be discovered, the best configuration achieves a mean FDE-Gym score of 0.56 and resolves only 14 of the 95 tasks (a score of at least 0.8 with no incident). Discovering unstated constraints is the primary bottleneck: performance drops sharply when models must uncover them without explicit guidance. Yet information discovery alone does not account for the gap: even on the 23 tasks where the best configuration obtains every key fact from stakeholders, it reaches a normalized business uplift of 0.8 or above on only 10. These results reveal a substantial gap between solving well-specified tasks and delivering effective AI systems for real customers.
items.title_ko: FDE-Gym: AI 배포의 마지막 마일 벤치마크
items.summary_ko: FDE-Gym은 기존 에이전트 벤치마크와 달리, 모호한 요구사항을 명확히 하고 실제 시스템에서 작업하며 숨겨진 제약 조건을 찾아내는 실제 고객 배포 시나리오를 반영한 새로운 벤치마크입니다.
items.why_ko: AI 에이전트의 실제 적용 가능성을 평가하는 데 있어 현실적인 과제를 제시하며, 현장 엔지니어(FDE)와 같은 실제 업무 환경에 최적화된 에이전트 개발을 촉진합니다.

items.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
items.body: Large language models (LLMs) are expanding from assisting scientific research and engineering to autonomously developing and improving AI systems, advancing AI for AI (AI4AI) as a pathway toward recursive self-improvement (RSI). Workflow-driven machine learning engineering (MLE) systems provide a practical path toward this pursuit through complex orchestration that manages long-horizon experimentation, while recent MLE systems adopt model-directed interaction, allowing models to autonomously organize experiments and adapt optimization strategies based on execution feedback. However, feedback from each experiment reflects several preceding decisions, and a long MLE run contains many such costly experiments. Training must therefore select useful supervision from long interaction trajectories and learn from intermediate outcomes. We propose a post-training method for autonomous long-horizon MLE optimization and apply it to train MLExpert, a 35B Mixture-of-Experts agentic model. We design the Kaggle-MLE Factory to construct executable tasks and an interaction harness for model-directed experimentation. Hierarchical agentic SFT transfers general tool-use and coding capabilities to MLE through outcome-guided supervision. Windowed Interaction RL (WIRL) treats the multi-turn decisions between successive experiment results as an execution window and assigns it a shared outcome-based reward. Asynchronous collection and policy correction support policy updates before the trajectory ends. On MLE-Bench Lite, MLExpert improves the average medal rate of the base model from 37.9% to 72.7%, achieving performance comparable to larger frontier models such as Kimi-K3 and GLM-5.3. Further experiments show that MLExpert improves performance on NatureBench Lite, agent scaffold optimization, and algorithm optimization, suggesting that the learned optimization capability generalizes to other tasks.
items.title_ko: MLExpert: 자율 기계 학습 엔지니어링을 위한 범용 에이전트 모델 개발
items.summary_ko: MLExpert는 대규모 언어 모델(LLM)이 과학 연구 및 엔지니어링 지원을 넘어 자율적으로 AI 시스템을 개발하고 개선하는 범용 에이전트 모델입니다. 장기적인 실험과 모델 중심 상호작용을 관리하는 복잡한 오케스트레이션을 통해 재귀적 자기 개선(RSI)을 추구합니다.
items.why_ko: AI가 스스로 AI 시스템을 설계하고 최적화하는 'AI for AI' 개념을 발전시키며, 자율적인 머신러닝 엔지니어링을 통해 AI 개발의 효율성과 속도를 획기적으로 향상시킬 수 있는 잠재력을 보여줍니다.

items.title: GeoState: Learning View-Decoupled Geometry States for 3D World Modeling
items.body: Recent 3D world models increasingly use features from geometry foundation models (GFMs) as predictive world states, benefiting from their rich geometric priors. However, the view dependence of these features entangles scene dynamics with camera-induced variation, making the resulting state evolution harder to predict. We propose GeoState, a view-decoupled geometry representation for predictive 3D world modeling that separates scene-state evolution from camera-dependent observation. Specifically, a scene tokenizer aggregates multi-view GFM features into a view-decoupled scene state, which a geometry decoder queries using camera rays. An autoregressive world model then predicts future scene states, while camera motion is modeled separately. The predicted states can therefore be decoded under either predicted or externally specified cameras, while retaining a single context-derived scale throughout the rollout without per-frame scale alignment. Experiments show that GeoState outperforms prior 3D world models on Waymo, supports geometrically consistent cross-view querying, and generalizes zero-shot to KITTI and nuScenes. Project page: https://hongchang-liu.github.io/GeoState-project-page/
items.title_ko: GeoState: 3D 월드 모델링을 위한 뷰 분리 기하학 상태 학습
items.summary_ko: 최신 3D 월드 모델은 기하학 파운데이션 모델(GFM)의 풍부한 기하학적 사전 지식을 예측 상태로 활용하지만, 뷰 의존성으로 인해 장면 역학이 카메라 유도 변화와 얽힙니다. GeoState는 장면 상태 진화와 카메라 의존적 관찰을 분리하여 예측 3D 월드 모델링을 위한 뷰 분리 기하학 표현을 제안합니다.
items.why_ko: 3D 월드 모델링에서 장면의 동적 변화를 더 정확하게 예측하고, 카메라 시점에 따른 변화와 실제 장면의 변화를 분리하여 모델의 안정성과 예측 능력을 향상시킵니다.

items.title: 3DCodeVerse: Exploring 3D Worlds as Code
items.body: We introduce 3DCodeVerse, a research ecosystem that enables coding agents to create editable and verifiable 3D content at scale. 3DCodeVerse comprises large-scale, high-quality datasets of executable 3D code, a coding harness for spatial reasoning and automated verification, and practical guidance for 3D coding. First, we construct 3DCodeVerse-2M, a large-scale curated dataset of standalone 3D executable code. We build this corpus by collecting open-source data, converting specialized representations, and generating new programs with coding agents. Each program is packaged with the source files and associated assets required for execution in its declared environment, along with available descriptions and verification records. Second, we develop the 3DCodeVerse Harness, a multi-agent directed acyclic graph framework for generating and refining 3D content. It uses execution checks, spatial measurements, and visual feedback to automatically evaluate and revise generated programs without human feedback during generation. Third, we conduct systematic empirical studies of 3D coding, establishing baselines with fine-tuned open models and deriving practical guidance through component-level analyses of our harness. Extensive experiments demonstrate that fine-tuning on our dataset significantly improves the 3D coding capabilities of open-source models. Notably, our 3DCodeVerse harness achieves a 90% win rate against Claude Design (3D Object) in pairwise human evaluations, when both are utilized by Claude Opus 5.5.
items.title_ko: 3DCodeVerse: 코드로 3D 세계 탐험을 위한 연구 생태계
items.summary_ko: 3DCodeVerse는 코딩 에이전트가 편집 가능하고 검증 가능한 3D 콘텐츠를 대규모로 생성할 수 있도록 지원하는 연구 생태계입니다. 실행 가능한 3D 코드의 대규모 고품질 데이터셋, 공간 추론 및 자동 검증을 위한 코딩 하네스, 그리고 3D 코딩에 대한 실용적인 지침을 포함합니다.
items.why_ko: 개발자들이 코드를 통해 3D 환경을 만들고 조작할 수 있는 새로운 패러다임을 제시하며, 3D 콘텐츠 생성 및 가상 세계 구축에 AI의 역할을 확장합니다.

items.title: Dexterity from Supervised Play
items.body: How can robots autonomously collect the contact-rich experience needed to learn dexterous manipulation? We present DSP: Dexterity from supervised play, a framework in which a robot learns a play policy from minutes of human play through behavior cloning, then deploys it autonomously to collect hours of interaction data to train a world model. During inference, the same play policy then guides model-predictive control (MPC) by proposing candidate action sequences for evaluation under the learned world model. To accelerate inference, we also introduce a method for distilling a closed-loop, goal-conditioned policy through self-play within the learned world model. We evaluate this framework on underactuated pushing and any-to-any in-hand pose reorientation with a multifingered hand, in simulation and real world. In real world experiment, our method outperforms hindsight behavior cloning by 69.6% in success rate and achieves comparable success to reinforcement learning with 490 times less interaction data. These results demonstrate that supervised play can autonomously collect interaction data, guide model-based planning, and enable policy learning without any task-specific demonstrations or sim-to-real transfer.
items.title_ko: 지도 학습 기반 플레이를 통한 로봇의 정교한 조작 능력 학습
items.summary_ko: DSP(Dexterity from Supervised Play)는 인간의 몇 분간의 플레이를 행동 복제를 통해 로봇이 플레이 정책을 학습하고, 이를 자율적으로 배포하여 수 시간의 상호작용 데이터를 수집하여 월드 모델을 훈련하는 프레임워크입니다.
items.why_ko: 로봇이 인간의 지도와 자율적인 데이터 수집을 통해 복잡하고 섬세한 조작 기술을 효율적으로 학습할 수 있는 방법을 제시하여, 실제 환경에서의 로봇 활용 가능성을 높입니다.

items.title: Lean Graph Search for Formal Theorem Proving
items.body: Retrieving relevant lemmas is crucial for formal theorem proving, enabling provers to build machine-checkable proofs from established mathematical results. Recent retrieval systems match library declarations to a target theorem or its intermediate proof steps, but make limited use of multi-hop dependencies among declarations. These dependencies can reveal supporting lemmas that are not necessarily lexically similar to the target theorem but recur in proofs of related problems. To this end, we propose LeanGraphSearch, a graph-based retrieval method for Lean 4 that constructs a graph from Mathlib's forward dependencies and traverses it to uncover supporting lemmas through multi-hop dependency chains. Specifically, LeanGraphSearch links each declaration to the premises it depends on, uses a graph-based ranking algorithm to propagate relevance from semantically matched declarations to their dependencies, and reranks the expanded candidates against the original query. Across two mathematical retrieval benchmarks, LeanGraphSearch improves recall by up to 12% over the strongest baseline, LeanSearch v2, on MathlibQR and increases coverage of complete annotated proof routes on MathlibMPR, covering up to 3.7% of extra groups. More importantly, we evaluate whether these retrieval gains translate into improved end-to-end theorem proving by integrating LeanGraphSearch into an iterative proving loop guided by Lean feedback. Across three theorem proving benchmarks, LeanGraphSearch improves pass rate at {8, 16, 32} reflection turns by as much as 40% compared to vanilla prover and at most 10% compared to LeanSearch v2, showing higher accuracy-cost efficiency. These findings highlight the value of dependency graph search for theorem proving and motivate further research on structure-aware search for proof discovery.

items.title: Robust Reinforcement Learning for Dynamic Treatment Regimes under Model and Measurement Uncertainty
items.body: We develop a robust reinforcement learning (RL) framework for learning adaptive treatment policies that generalize across patients and remain reliable under errors in the measured biomarker and shifts in the disease dynamics. By modeling the patient as a hidden context, we address generalization and robustness in a unified manner through robust contextual Markov decision processes. Applying our framework to adaptive therapy for metastatic prostate cancer in a simulator calibrated to clinical data, we obtain generalizable and robust policies that substantially outperform the existing adaptive therapy method. In particular, we attain robustness with almost no loss of performance when the biomarker is accurate and the disease evolves as anticipated, and find that the resulting policy Pareto-dominates the existing method across a diverse array of scenarios. Our findings suggest that robust RL holds great promise as a principled methodology for learning reliable adaptive treatment policies.
items.title_ko: 모델 및 측정 불확실성 하의 동적 치료 요법을 위한 강건한 강화 학습
items.summary_ko: 환자를 숨겨진 컨텍스트로 모델링하여 강건한 컨텍스트 마르코프 의사 결정 프로세스를 통해 동적 치료 정책 학습의 일반화 및 강건성을 다루는 강화 학습 프레임워크가 개발되었습니다. 전립선암 적응형 치료 시뮬레이터에 적용되어 임상 데이터에 맞춰 검증되었습니다.
items.why_ko: 의료 분야에서 AI를 활용한 개인 맞춤형 치료 정책 개발의 신뢰성과 효율성을 높이며, 실제 임상 환경에서 발생할 수 있는 불확실성에 강건한 AI 시스템 구축의 가능성을 제시합니다.

items.title: Evaluation Awareness Beyond English: Do LLMs Act Differently When Tested in Indic Languages?
items.body: Large language models (LLMs) can often tell when they are being tested. This ability, known as evaluation awareness, can lead models to act more cautiously during safety evaluations than in real use. Existing work has studied evaluation awareness almost entirely in English, although models serve users in many languages. Indic languages are spoken by over a billion people, yet evaluation awareness remains almost entirely unstudied in them. We test four instruction-tuned models from three families in five Indic languages alongside English. A set of cues varies whether the model is told that it is monitored and whether the monitoring is a safety test. Models refuse harmful requests more often when they are told that they are being tested. This increase appears in all four models and all six languages. In Indic languages, refusal of harmful requests rises by 14.4 percentage points on average. The test cue also brings Indic refusal of harmful requests level with English, but raises refusal of benign Indic requests from 6.9% to 11.3%. We release all 47,880 judged responses to support further work. These results suggest that safety evaluations in Indic languages may not reflect how models treat their everyday users.
items.title_ko: 영어 외 언어에서의 평가 인식: LLM이 인도어 테스트 시 다르게 행동하는가?
items.summary_ko: LLM이 자신이 테스트 중임을 인지하는 '평가 인식' 능력은 주로 영어에서 연구되었지만, 인도어에서는 거의 연구되지 않았습니다. 이 연구는 세 가지 계열의 네 가지 지시 튜닝 모델이 인도어 테스트에서 다르게 행동하는지 여부를 탐구합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 '평가 인식'이라는 중요한 특성이 언어별로 어떻게 다른 영향을 미치는지 밝혀내어, 비영어권 사용자에게 더 안전하고 공정한 AI 서비스를 제공하기 위한 연구 방향을 제시합니다.

items.title: KnowGPO: Knowledge-Grouped Policy Optimization for Search Agents
items.body: Deep search agents solve knowledge-intensive tasks through long-horizon, multi-turn interactions, where assigning credit to individual search decisions is fundamentally difficult. Outcome-based reinforcement learning provides only a single terminal reward shared across an entire trajectory. Recent process-supervision methods aim to assign credit at finer granularity, but they typically anchor credit to either surface-level trajectory states or model-internal signals, both of which become unreliable in deep search where observations are heterogeneous and retrieved contexts are long and noisy. We propose KnowGPO, a reinforcement learning framework that aligns trajectories by the task-relevant knowledge they have acquired rather than by their surface observations. For each query, KnowGPO decomposes the information required to derive the answer into atomic knowledge conditions, and represents the state of a trajectory at each step by the subset of conditions it has satisfied. Trajectories sharing the same knowledge state are grouped for within-group comparison, and the incremental knowledge gain between consecutive steps serves as an environment-grounded process reward. Experiments on Xbench, BrowseComp-ZH, and GAIA show KnowGPO consistently outperforms outcome-only (GRPO) and process-supervision baselines (GiGPO, IGPO) by 3.8 to 4.2 points, with our 8B model rivaling or exceeding most 32B open-source systems.
items.title_ko: KnowGPO: 검색 에이전트를 위한 지식 그룹화 정책 최적화
items.summary_ko: 지식 집약적 작업을 해결하는 심층 검색 에이전트에서 개별 검색 결정에 대한 신용 할당은 어렵습니다. KnowGPO는 단일 최종 보상에 의존하는 기존 방식을 개선하여, 지식 그룹 기반의 정책 최적화를 통해 장기적인 상호작용에서 신용 할당의 정확도를 높입니다.
items.why_ko: 복잡한 지식 기반 작업을 수행하는 LLM 에이전트의 의사결정 과정을 개선하고, 장기적인 추론과정에서 발생하는 신용 할당 문제를 해결하여 에이전트의 성능을 향상시킵니다.

items.title: Designing Transformers for Continuous Diffusion Language Models
items.body: Continuous diffusion language models (CDLMs) offer an alternative approach to parallel language generation; however, most existing studies directly use transformer architectures from either causal large language models (LLMs) or Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) for image generation, which were not optimized for CDLMs. In this paper, we conduct a systematic study on Transformer architectures for CDLMs and introduce Language Diffusion Transformer (LangDiT), combining feature and query-key normalization, wider noise conditioning, likelihood-shortcut gradient routing and calibration, and confidence-gated training self-conditioning. LangDiT significantly reduces generation perplexity in matched LangFlow comparisons, establishing a new state of the art in continuous language generation across different model formulations. Using LangFlow as a representative CDLM, LangDiT as a plug-and-play backbone leads to a new state-of-the-art model with a generation perplexity (GenPPL) of 21.72 using 1024 NFEs and 44.72 GenPPL using 128 NFEs on the unconditional generation of 1024-token sequences on the OpenWebText dataset. When adapted to Plaid-style CDLM formulations, LangDiT results in a new leading GenPPL of 11.33 using 1024 denoising NFEs, and 27.51 GenPPL using 128 denoising NFEs. These gains are achieved while retaining each model's underlying representation, training objective, and inference sampler, isolating transformer architecture as a fundamental source of improvement. Our study identifies architectural design as an important source of improvement in continuous diffusion language models.
items.title_ko: 연속 확산 언어 모델을 위한 트랜스포머 설계: LangDiT 제안
items.summary_ko: 연속 확산 언어 모델(CDLM)은 병렬 언어 생성의 대안을 제공하지만, 기존 연구들은 대부분 인과적 LLM이나 이미지 생성 DiT의 트랜스포머 아키텍처를 직접 사용합니다. 이 연구는 CDLM을 위한 트랜스포머 아키텍처를 체계적으로 연구하여 Language Diffusion Transformer (LangDiT)를 제안합니다.
items.why_ko: 연속 확산 언어 모델에 최적화된 트랜스포머 아키텍처를 제안하여, 병렬 언어 생성의 효율성과 품질을 향상시키고, 새로운 LLM 아키텍처 연구의 방향을 제시합니다.

items.title: ACEdit: Stable Multi-Turn Image Editing via Asymmetric Conditioning
items.body: Image editing models produce impressive results for individual edits, but their quality often deteriorates over multiple editing turns. Each editing turn introduces small distribution shifts that accumulate over successive edits, creating a gap between the input distributions encountered during the editor's original training and multi-turn inference. We introduce a training scheme that makes multi-turn image editing stable under this accumulating distribution shift. A key is to force the editor to operate on its own outputs from previous editing turns during training, bringing the principle of Self-Forcing to image editing. The main challenge is that self-generated editing trajectories deviate from ground-truth trajectories, making direct supervision unreliable. We address this challenge through a distillation objective that leverages a teacher image editor to provide a reliable training signal when the model operates on its own previous outputs. We introduce an asymmetric conditioning scheme: while the student performs edits sequentially on its own outputs, the teacher remains anchored to the original clean image and receives a compound editing instruction. Experiments show substantially reduced degradation over long multi-turn sequences while maintaining editing quality and instruction adherence.
items.title_ko: ACEdit: 비대칭 조건화를 통한 안정적인 다중 턴 이미지 편집
items.summary_ko: 이미지 편집 모델은 단일 편집에서 인상적인 결과를 내지만, 여러 번의 편집 턴이 반복될수록 품질이 저하됩니다. ACEdit은 편집 턴마다 발생하는 분포 변화를 안정화하는 훈련 방식을 도입하여, 비대칭 조건화를 통해 다중 턴 이미지 편집의 안정성을 확보합니다.
items.why_ko: 다중 턴 이미지 편집의 고질적인 문제인 품질 저하를 해결하여, 사용자가 여러 단계를 거쳐 이미지를 정교하게 편집할 수 있도록 지원하며 실용적인 이미지 생성 AI의 활용성을 높입니다.

items.title: Twice Upon a Time: Complementary Representations for Time-Series Reasoning
items.body: Time Series Language Models (TSLMs) enable language-based understanding and reasoning over temporal data, yet a fundamental question remains: what information should their time-series representations preserve, and what variation should they factor out? Existing TSLMs typically expose the language model to a single representation, imposing a fixed inductive bias across downstream tasks. We instead introduce complementary representations as a design principle for time-series reasoning. Our model combines two visual views: line plots preserve absolute measurements and the observed coordinate frame, while normalized delay embeddings factor out positive amplitude rescaling and offsets while exposing temporal structure. Dedicated visual encoders integrate both views into a shared language model through visual tokens and multi-level feature fusion. Evaluation-time interventions verify that the two views exhibit distinct invariance profiles, while single-view ablations show that their combination is particularly beneficial beyond basic perception, with the large gains in prediction and reasoning. Built on Qwen3-VL-8B, our dual-view model improves overall TSRBench accuracy from 44.5% with line plots alone to 53.2%, substantially exceeding the strongest evaluated dedicated TSLM baseline at 36.7%. It further achieves 89.9% accuracy on TSExam and 86.8% numerical accuracy on multivariate ChatTS alignment. Together, these results demonstrate that complementary representations provide an effective design principle for general-purpose TSLMs, enabling models to exploit temporal structure without sacrificing access to the original measurement frame.
items.title_ko: Twice Upon a Time: 시계열 추론을 위한 상호 보완적 표현
items.summary_ko: 시계열 언어 모델(TSLM)은 시간 데이터에 대한 언어 기반 이해와 추론을 가능하게 하지만, 시계열 표현이 어떤 정보를 보존하고 어떤 변화를 제거해야 하는지에 대한 질문이 남아있습니다. 이 연구는 '상호 보완적 표현'을 시계열 추론의 설계 원칙으로 도입합니다.
items.why_ko: 시계열 데이터에서 언어 모델의 추론 능력을 향상시키기 위한 새로운 표현 방식을 제시하며, 다양한 시계열 작업에 더 효과적으로 적용될 수 있는 모델 개발에 기여합니다.

items.title: Training Reasoning Models to Generate Diverse Scientific Ideas
items.body: One of the first steps of a research pipeline is generating ideas. Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used to automate this step, but most of this work optimizes the quality of individual ideas, while overlooking diversity. In our work, we study document-grounded ideation, focusing on increasing the diversity of LLM generated ideas and ensuring they are high quality. Given prior papers, a model must propose a set of ideas that are each high-quality and clearly distinct from one another, while also being grounded in the input documents. To optimize for this, we propose training with a set-level reinforcement learning objective. In our setup, in a single generation, the model writes K structured idea cards grounded in the source papers, and the set is scored jointly, where each idea's quality is weighted by its distance from the ideas written before it. This teaches the model to steer each new idea away from its predecessors. We show that our trained 8B model achieves higher creative utility (a measure combining quality and diversity) than Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-6 Astra on our contamination-free benchmark. In a pilot human study with four experts, our sets are judged as promising as Claude Opus 4.8's and contain marginally more unique ideas. When a coding agent runs proof-of-concept experiments on the ideas, our model's success@k is comparable to Claude Opus 4.8's, so we see that the added diversity does not cost any executability.
items.title_ko: 다양한 과학적 아이디어 생성을 위한 추론 모델 훈련
items.summary_ko: 연구 파이프라인의 첫 단계인 아이디어 생성에 LLM이 활용되고 있지만, 대부분은 개별 아이디어의 품질에만 초점을 맞춥니다. 이 연구는 문서 기반 아이디어 생성에서 LLM이 고품질이면서도 다양한 아이디어를 생성하도록 훈련하는 방법을 탐구합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM이 단순히 고품질 아이디어를 넘어 창의적이고 다양한 아이디어를 생성하도록 훈련하는 방법을 제시하여, 과학 연구 및 문제 해결 과정에서 LLM의 활용 가치를 높입니다.

items.title: Learning Self-Orchestration in Decentralized Agent Swarms
items.body: The capabilities of an agent swarm depend on both its individual members and how they coordinate. Yet existing multi-agent systems often train agents within fixed orchestration structures, separating the learning of individual capabilities from the organization of collective behavior. We introduce market-based post-training (MPT), a framework for jointly learning action policies and self-orchestration in decentralized agent swarms. Agents express their willingness to participate through bids, which determine who acts and how collective outcomes provide local training credit. Learning both action and bidding behavior allows individual capabilities and patterns of participation to adapt together without a central coordinating agent. We evaluate MPT on embodied crafting, robot navigation, and deep research. Results show gains over monolithic post-training and confirm that agent participation indeed evolves with learning. With the same post-trained action policies, learned self-orchestration outperforms alternative coordination strategies. Ablations show that both action and bidding benefit from learning, and that learned bids provide more effective action-training signals. Beyond the original training objectives, trained swarms adapt faster to related tasks and achieve better performance with larger populations at inference time. Larger populations also suffer smaller performance losses under agent dropout, demonstrating that learned self-orchestration supports reuse, scaling, and robustness in decentralized agent swarms. Code and trained models are available at https://github.com/Embodied-Minds-Lab/MPT.
items.title_ko: 탈중앙화 에이전트 스웜의 자기 조직화 학습
items.summary_ko: 기존 멀티 에이전트 시스템은 고정된 조직 구조 내에서 에이전트를 훈련하여 개별 능력 학습과 집단 행동 조직을 분리합니다. 이 연구는 탈중앙화 에이전트 스웜에서 행동 정책과 자기 조직화를 공동으로 학습하는 시장 기반 후처리(MPT) 프레임워크를 제안합니다.
items.why_ko: 분산된 AI 에이전트들이 스스로 협력하고 조직화하는 능력을 학습하게 함으로써, 복잡하고 변화하는 환경에서 더 효율적이고 유연한 다중 에이전트 시스템을 구축할 수 있습니다.

items.title: AVC-Reward: Event-Centric Audio-Video Consistency Evaluation
items.body: As joint audio-video generation models become more capable, they can generate audio-visual scenes exhibiting three forms of complexity: multi-event composition, multi-layer audio mixture, and asymmetric cross-modal relations. However, current evaluations largely reuse metrics from earlier simple and unidirectional tasks. They typically evaluate an audio-video clip as a whole and rely on simple predefined relations, making them unsuitable for these increasingly complex scenes. We propose an event-centric evaluation framework that disentangles audio and visual events at the event level, analyzes each event independently, cross-validates relations across modalities, and aggregates the judgments into a coarse-to-fine, three-level consistency metric. The metric assesses global narrative harmony, event-level temporal synchronization, and fine-grained attribute alignment, providing a general formulation for audio-video consistency evaluation across diverse generation settings and cross-modal relations. We instantiate the metric as AVC-Reward, a trainable audio-video reward model. To evaluate the agreement between automatic judgments and human perception across generation paradigms and relation complexities, we construct AVC-Benchmark, which is primarily built from diverse positive and negative samples generated by various types of audio-video generation models. AVC-Reward achieves state-of-the-art alignment with human judgment among automatic methods, provides interpretable rationales that localize failures, and improves the audio-video consistency of a joint generation model when used as an online reinforcement-learning signal. Project page: https://tsuki0512.github.io/AVC-Reward.github.io/
items.title_ko: AVC-Reward: 이벤트 중심 오디오-비디오 일관성 평가
items.summary_ko: 오디오-비디오 생성 모델이 복잡한 멀티 이벤트 구성, 멀티 레이어 오디오 혼합, 비대칭 교차 모달 관계를 처리할 수 있게 됨에 따라, 기존의 단순하고 단방향적인 평가 지표로는 부족합니다. AVC-Reward는 이벤트 기반 오디오-비디오 일관성 평가를 제안합니다.
