items.why_ko: 점점 더 복잡해지는 오디오-비디오 생성 모델의 품질을 정확하게 평가하기 위한 새로운 프레임워크를 제시하며, 멀티모달 AI의 발전과 신뢰성 확보에 기여합니다.

items.title: A team of Gemini 4 Argon agents beats Minecraft
items.body: We placed four Gemini 4 Argon agents in a sandboxed Minecraft survival world and gave them one goal: defeat the Ender Dragon. Each agent controlled a player via an open-source library called Mineflayer and coordinated with its teammates through in-game chat and shared memory. No one assigned roles or wrote game logic. The agents planned, wrote, and debugged every program themselves. Researchers could watch the run on a live dashboard and pause or stop it at any time, but they had no cause to intervene. Starting from a randomly generated world on Easy difficulty, the team wrote 2,783 programs and defeated the dragon in 27 hours and 14 minutes, dying 605 times along the way. To our knowledge, this is the first end-to-end autonomous completion of Minecraft by AI agents, achieved using only the standard Mineflayer library without pre-scouted seeds or other game-specific tools written by humans. Winning required the agents to keep a coherent plan across thousands of dependent steps for more than a day. Complex real-world software engineering and enterprise tasks demand the same long-horizon coding and multi-agent coordination. We describe the setup, how the run unfolded, the team's strategies (dividing the work, sharing what they learned, recovering each other's items), and the limits of the result.
items.title_ko: Gemini 4 Argon 에이전트 팀, 마인크래프트 클리어
items.summary_ko: 4개의 Gemini 4 Argon 에이전트 팀이 샌드박스 마인크래프트 서바이벌 모드에서 엔더 드래곤을 물리치는 데 성공했습니다. 에이전트들은 사전 역할 할당이나 게임 로직 없이 자체적으로 계획, 코딩, 디버깅을 수행하며 인게임 채팅과 공유 메모리를 통해 협력했습니다.
items.why_ko: 복잡한 개방형 게임 환경에서 다중 LLM 에이전트의 뛰어난 자율성, 협업 능력, 문제 해결 능력을 보여주며, 이는 실제 세계의 복합적인 작업을 해결하는 에이전트 시스템 개발에 큰 진전을 의미합니다.

items.title: Learning to Steer LLM Agents and Multi-Agent Systems
items.body: Large language model (LLM)-based agents and multi-agent systems increasingly tackle complex tasks through long-horizon tool use and inter-agent collaboration. However, these systems are prone to deviating from the overall goal as execution unfolds, which wastes execution resources and leads to undesired outcomes, a failure termed goal drift. In this work, we propose a steering agent that supervises execution on the fly and steers the system back on track when drift occurs. The steering agent observes the execution context, deciding when to intervene with a low-cost fast path and how to intervene with a high-cost slow path. To unlock its steering intelligence, the ability to assess goal drift and generate effective interventions, we jointly train the two paths with reinforcement learning, combining a pairwise ranking objective with group-relative policy optimization (GRPO). Experiments on information-seeking search tasks show that the steering agent provides effective supervision for both single-agent and multi-agent systems, improving their performance and efficiency. The learned steering intelligence generalizes to out-of-domain tasks, transfers to unseen executors, and supports controllable intervention frequency without retraining.
items.title_ko: LLM 에이전트 및 다중 에이전트 시스템 조종 학습
items.summary_ko: LLM 기반 에이전트와 다중 에이전트 시스템은 복잡한 작업을 수행하지만, '목표 이탈(goal drift)' 경향이 있어 자원 낭비와 원치 않는 결과로 이어질 수 있습니다. 이 연구는 실행 중 목표 이탈을 감지하고 시스템을 다시 제어하는 '조종 에이전트'를 제안합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM 에이전트가 장기적인 작업을 수행할 때 발생할 수 있는 목표 이탈 문제를 해결하여, 에이전트 시스템의 안정성과 신뢰성을 높이는 실용적인 방안을 제시합니다.

items.title: MindEval2: Clinically Grounded Patients and Rubrics for Evaluating Language Models in Mental Health Support
items.body: With people increasingly turning to AI chatbots for mental health support, the need to evaluate these tools is becoming more pressing. Recent benchmarks attempt to mimic a realistic setting by simulating multi-turn interactions with synthetic patients and evaluating them with an LLM-as-a-judge. However, the usefulness of these methods is limited because simulated patients can be overly forthcoming and self-reflective, and judgments typically involve opaque Likert scales with unclear practical utility. To bridge these gaps, we introduce MindEval2, an evaluation framework that consists of two components: Mental Health Quality Rubrics (MHQR), for evaluation, and MindSim, for patient simulation. For MHQR, we collaborate with PhD-level psychologists to develop a set of rubrics that break down response quality into explicit operational criteria that are more interpretable and actionable than existing evaluation taxonomies. MindSim, in turn, is an LLM harness that combines carefully-designed patient profiles with tools, enabling more varied, challenging, and realistic interactions than existing baselines. The harness also contains a memory component that is updated between each interaction, enabling MindEval2 to model the longitudinal aspect of mental health. We evaluate 18 proprietary and open-weight models on MindEval2, finding that while frontier models have largely improved on issues related to surface level quality and boundaries, guidance calibration remains the dominant failure mode across all models, accounting for most of the quality gap.
items.title_ko: MindEval2: 정신 건강 지원 LLM 평가를 위한 임상 기반 환자 및 루브릭
items.summary_ko: AI 챗봇의 정신 건강 지원 활용이 증가함에 따라, 이 도구들의 평가 필요성이 커지고 있습니다. MindEval2는 지나치게 솔직하고 자기 성찰적인 시뮬레이션 환자 및 불투명한 리커트 척도에 의존하는 기존 벤치마크의 한계를 극복하기 위해, 임상적으로 근거한 환자와 루브릭을 제시합니다.
items.why_ko: AI 기반 정신 건강 지원 도구의 실용적이고 윤리적인 평가를 위한 더 현실적이고 엄격한 표준을 제시하며, 사용자에게 안전하고 효과적인 AI 상담을 제공하는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: Grid-Bench: Can LLMs Predict How Discrete Worlds Change?
items.body: Spatial instructions describe how to move objects, transform regions, or modify their surroundings. When several operations are applied in sequence, each acts on a configuration shaped by earlier changes. How accurately can large language models (LLMs) predict the resulting spatial state? We introduce Grid-Bench, an executable benchmark in which eight families of operations transform discrete worlds represented as two-, three-, and four-dimensional grids. Given an initial grid, explicit rules, and an event history expressed as text, a model predicts the complete final grid. Reference execution makes every predicted value checkable, supporting comparisons across spatial operations, history lengths, and workloads. Evaluating six LLMs shows that complete-state accuracy falls sharply as histories grow, with substantial divergence among models that perform similarly on single events. Models with similar exact-match accuracy can nevertheless differ substantially in the number of incorrect cells on shared instances. Even over long histories, some models recover many correct changes beyond what copying the initial state would yield. Grid-Bench makes both complete recovery and these differences in returned states directly measurable across a range of spatial conditions.
items.title_ko: Grid-Bench: LLM이 이산 세계의 변화를 예측할 수 있는가?
items.summary_ko: 공간 명령이 순차적으로 적용될 때 LLM이 결과적인 공간 상태를 얼마나 정확하게 예측할 수 있는지 평가하기 위해 Grid-Bench 벤치마크가 도입되었습니다. 이 벤치마크는 2D, 3D, 4D 그리드로 표현된 이산 세계를 변환하는 여덟 가지 유형의 작업을 포함합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM이 복잡한 공간 추론 및 순차적 변화 예측 능력을 평가하는 새로운 벤치마크를 제공하여, AI의 물리적 세계 모델링 및 시뮬레이션 능력을 발전시키는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: Knowledge That Is Linear Before Fine-Tuning Generalizes After It
items.body: Not all facts a language model can recall support further learning equally well. We distinguish active facts, which support generalization beyond their own recall, from inert facts, which can be recalled but do not support such generalization in a given task. We study this distinction by constructing new relations from existing ones. Take the relation that maps a place to its continent (Paris -> Europe) and assign each of its answers an arbitrary new label (Europe -> crab, Asia -> zebra). The new relation then maps Paris -> crab. We fine-tune the model on the new relation for a subset of subjects, without telling it the original relation or the relabeling rule, and test whether it assigns the corresponding labels to held-out subjects that share an answer in the original relation. Having learned Paris -> crab, does it answer Munich -> crab? Across eleven language models and 70 relations, how linearly readable the original relation is in pretrained representations strongly predicts this generalization. Within each model, the two correlate across relations at Pearson r = 0.87 to 0.92. This association persists when controlling, separately and jointly, for the number of fine-tuning subjects and answers, the model's accuracy on the original relation, and how often the subjects occur in pretraining text. It is also robust to re-randomizing the label assignment and fine-tuning seed, and to replacing the animal labels with labels from thirteen other semantic categories. When we map a fine-tuned model's wrong label back to the original answer it was assigned to, Munich -> zebra becomes Munich -> Asia. Answers recovered this way are more often among the linear probe's top answers for the subject than among the pretrained model's own. Whether a new relation generalizes depends less on whether its facts can be recalled than on how readily their shared structure can be read out linearly.
items.title_ko: 미세 조정 전 선형적인 지식은 미세 조정 후에도 일반화된다
items.summary_ko: 언어 모델이 기억할 수 있는 모든 사실이 추가 학습을 동일하게 잘 지원하는 것은 아닙니다. 이 연구는 '활성 사실'과 '비활성 사실'을 구분하고, 기존 관계에서 새로운 관계를 구성하여 미세 조정 전 선형적이었던 지식이 미세 조정 후에도 일반화되는 경향을 탐구합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 지식 학습과 일반화 능력에 대한 근본적인 이해를 돕고, 효율적인 미세 조정을 통해 모델의 성능을 향상시키는 방법을 모색하는 데 중요한 통찰을 제공합니다.

items.title: AI Consilium: a Benchmark of LLM Clinical Multidisciplinary Second Opinions
items.body: Large language models (LLMs) can generate differential diagnoses for complex cases, but a useful second opinion must also be factually grounded, clinically coherent, actionable, and safe. We developed a multidimensional benchmark using 300 diagnostically resolved NEJM--MedQA cases: 110 for physician reference ratings and Judge calibration and 190 for held-out evaluation. Eight single-model pipelines generated independent role-specific opinions and interactive-consilium reports under free-form and structured clinical-reasoning conditions. A physician-calibrated LLM Judge evaluated 3,040 final reports and the corresponding structured primary-role outputs. Model identity separated report quality more strongly than response format. Structured final reports had higher overall mean scores in seven of eight model pipelines, with their clearest advantage in management (2.740 vs. 2.436). Compared with the structured pre-consilium primary-role opinion, the complete structured synthesis had higher pooled scores across all five shared criteria, with the largest increases in problem prioritization, factual grounding, and reasoning coherence. GPT-5.6-Sol led every evaluated component and reached consensus in the fewest review rounds. These findings show that the benchmark can distinguish model capability, the contribution of multidisciplinary synthesis, criterion-specific effects of response structure, deliberation dynamics, and inference requirements within one common-case evaluation.
items.title_ko: AI Consilium: LLM 임상 다학제 2차 소견 벤치마크
items.summary_ko: LLM이 복잡한 임상 사례에 대한 감별 진단을 생성할 수 있지만, 유용한 2차 소견은 사실에 기반하고 임상적으로 일관성 있으며 실행 가능하고 안전해야 합니다. AI Consilium은 300개의 진단이 해결된 NEJM-MedQA 사례를 사용하여 이러한 다차원적 평가를 위한 벤치마크를 개발했습니다.
items.why_ko: 의료 분야에서 LLM의 진단 보조 능력을 평가하는 엄격하고 다각적인 벤치마크를 제공하여, AI 기반 의료 시스템의 신뢰성과 안전성을 확보하는 데 중요한 역할을 합니다.

items.title: Private Retrieval Augmented Generation via Random Projection
items.body: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) enhances the capabilities of large language models (LLMs) by querying external structured knowledge. However, it can also introduce privacy risks by leaking sensitive information from the retrieval datastore. We propose a simple method to preserve datastore privacy in RAG systems via random projection. By applying the same projection to both datastore embeddings and query embeddings, our method provably preserves semantic similarity between queries and retrieved items while substantially mitigating data extraction attacks. Across multiple RAG architectures and datasets, we show that this lightweight approach achieves superior retrieval and generation performance compared to prior methods which leverage formal differential privacy (DP) guarantees, while exhibiting comparable empirical privacy under strong attack models. Our results for the first time suggest that random projection can serve as a competitive and practical baseline for privacy-preserving RAG systems.
items.title_ko: 랜덤 투영을 통한 RAG 시스템의 사설 정보 검색 강화
items.summary_ko: 검색 증강 생성(RAG)은 LLM의 능력을 향상시키지만, 검색 데이터스토어에서 민감한 정보를 유출할 수 있습니다. 이 연구는 랜덤 투영을 통해 RAG 시스템에서 데이터스토어 프라이버시를 보호하는 간단한 방법을 제안합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM 기반 RAG 시스템에서 사용자 프라이버시를 보호하면서도 검색 성능을 유지하는 실용적인 방법을 제시하여, 기업 및 민감 데이터를 다루는 AI 서비스의 보안성을 강화합니다.

items.title: Backward Compatibility in Zero-Bit Neural Audio Watermarking
items.body:
Neural watermarking systems are typically trained as tightly coupled embedder-detector pairs and implicitly assume static deployment. In real-world deployments, embedders and detectors are frequently updated and selectively decoupled for security and versioning purposes, which can break detection in previously embedded content and, more critically, increase false-positive rates on embedders that a given detector is intentionally not intended to recognize.
In this paper the concept of backward compatibility in zero-bit audio watermarking is formalized. A training framework is proposed that pairs a new detector with a sequence of frozen legacy embedders (its legacy chain), using a performance-weighted sampling strategy so that the detector retains accuracy across all earlier versions. This coupling, while necessary for backward compatibility, is shown to induce an embedder-collapse effect that catastrophically degrades the true negative rate (TNR) against out-of-chain embedders. To counteract this, a Angular Diversity Loss (ADL) is introduced that explicitly forces each new embedder to occupy a distinct region of the output space. The combined approach restores near-perfect TNR with no measurable cost to detection accuracy or perceptual audio quality.
items.title_ko: 제로 비트 신경 오디오 워터마킹의 하위 호환성
items.summary_ko: 신경 워터마킹 시스템은 일반적으로 긴밀하게 결합된 임베더-디텍터 쌍으로 훈련되며 정적 배포를 가정합니다. 하지만 실제 환경에서는 임베더와 디텍터가 자주 업데이트되고 선택적으로 분리되어 이전 콘텐츠의 감지 실패 및 오탐률 증가 문제를 야기합니다. 이 연구는 하위 호환성 개념을 도입합니다.
items.why_ko: 오디오 워터마킹 기술의 실제 적용성을 높이기 위해 버전 관리 및 보안 업데이트 시 발생하는 호환성 문제를 해결하는 방법을 제시하여, AI 기반 미디어 보안 기술의 실용화를 촉진합니다.

items.title: Multi-Target Few-Shot Prompting with Diffusion Language Models
items.body: Few-shot prompting is useful when instructions and rewards are hard to specify. One such application is editing by example, where a demonstrated formatting change or API migration may need to be applied across multiple sites. However, such edits often depend on both left and right context, making generation with causal autoregressive models awkward. We therefore introduce multi-target few-shot prompting with diffusion language models, where examples guide the infilling of multiple masked regions within a shared canvas. To address the known challenge of reliably following demonstrations in few-shot prompting, we further leverage selective masking of the canvas to derive a likelihood-ratio reward that favors example-supported infills. Across few-shot prompting benchmarks and software refactoring case studies, we find that demonstrations improve infilling accuracy, with example guidance yielding further gains in several settings.
items.title_ko: 확산 언어 모델을 이용한 다중 목표 Few-Shot 프롬프팅
items.summary_ko: 명령어와 보상을 지정하기 어려운 경우 Few-Shot 프롬프팅이 유용합니다. 이 연구는 확산 언어 모델을 활용한 다중 목표 Few-Shot 프롬프팅을 소개하여, 여러 마스크된 영역의 인필링(infilling)에 예제를 통해 가이드하는 방법을 제안합니다.
items.why_ko: 복잡한 텍스트 편집이나 API 마이그레이션과 같이 여러 위치에 동일한 변경 사항을 적용해야 하는 작업에서, 확산 언어 모델을 통해 효율적인 Few-Shot 프롬프팅을 가능하게 합니다.

items.title: Towards Continual Learning: Mitigating Forgetting With Subspace Tuning
items.body: Large language models (LLMs) acquire new skills through fine-tuning, but it can destroy capabilities they already have: catastrophic forgetting remains a central obstacle to continual learning in LLMs. Recent works connect forgetting to how far, and along which directions, fine-tuning moves the weights. On-policy methods such as reinforcement learning and on-policy distillation avoid updating the principal singular directions of weight matrices and thus forget less. In contrast, SFT concentrates updates along these directions and is susceptible to catastrophic forgetting. In this work, we introduce Subspace Tuning (SST), which restricts each weight update to the bottom singular subspace, eliminating changes along the principal directions. SST is optimizer-agnostic and composes well with fine-tuning recipes including SFT and self-distillation. SST combines tight subspace protection, dense gradient estimation, and a simple refresh mechanism, enabling stronger learning than prior orthogonal fine-tuning methods. With these mechanisms, protecting as much as 99\% of the weight subspace substantially improves retention while preserving strong target-task performance. This behavior strengthens with model and data size and nearly eliminates forgetting in the large-model regime. SST also keeps the model close to its base distribution, inducing $2$--$4\times$ less KL drift than the baseline recipes. Overall, SST advances the learning--forgetting Pareto frontier, making it a practical default for fine-tuning pre-trained language models.
items.title_ko: 연속 학습을 향하여: 부분공간 튜닝으로 망각 완화
items.summary_ko: LLM은 미세 조정을 통해 새로운 기술을 습득하지만, 이 과정에서 기존 능력을 파괴하는 치명적 망각(catastrophic forgetting)이 발생합니다. 이 연구는 가중치 이동 방향과 정도를 분석하여 온-정책(on-policy) 방법이 망각을 덜 유발한다는 점에 주목하고, 부분공간 튜닝을 통해 망각을 완화하는 방법을 제안합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 '치명적 망각' 문제를 해결하고, 모델이 새로운 지식을 학습하면서 기존 지식을 유지할 수 있는 효율적인 연속 학습 방법을 제시하여, 모델의 수명과 활용성을 높입니다.

items.title: CAT-alyzing Honesty: Continuous Adversarial Training for Transferable LLM Honesty
items.body: Large language models (LLMs) are becoming prevalent in scenarios where honesty is critical. However, despite alignment training, these models still exhibit dishonest behaviour, such as outputting claims that contradict some knowledge or are not supported by what is accessible in context. We introduce Continuous Adversarial Training for Consistent Honesty (CATCH), inspired by a method originally developed to robustly refuse harmful queries. CATCH trains the model towards an honest answer and away from a dishonest one while maintaining the model's capabilities. We evaluate two architectures (Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct and Qwen3-3.6-27B). We show that trained with only hundreds of targets built from self-reporting scenarios, CATCH learns an honest behaviour that robustly generalizes and transfers across distinct benchmarks. It consistently reduces dishonesty under pressure on MASK, increases confessions in the multi-agent game of Among Us, and improves the discovery rates of the model's hidden behaviours in AuditBench. We show that CATCH outperforms prompting and supervised fine-tuning in improving honesty, and it is on par with state-of-the-art honesty activation steering. However, CATCH surpasses honesty steering in maintaining utility, thanks to a novel choice of utility data.
items.title_ko: CAT-alyzing Honesty: 전이 가능한 LLM 정직성을 위한 지속적 적대적 훈련
items.summary_ko: LLM이 정직성을 요구하는 시나리오에서 널리 사용되지만, 정렬 훈련에도 불구하고 지식과 모순되거나 컨텍스트에 없는 주장을 하는 등 부정직한 행동을 보입니다. CATCH(Continuous Adversarial Training for Consistent Honesty)는 유해한 쿼리 거부 방법에서 영감을 받아, 일관된 정직성을 위한 지속적인 적대적 훈련 방식을 제안합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 신뢰성과 안전성을 높이는 핵심 요소인 '정직성'을 강화하기 위한 새로운 훈련 방식을 제시하며, 모델이 잘못된 정보를 생성하는 것을 효과적으로 방지하는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: EliteReplay: Preserving Diverse Solutions in RL Post-Training via Quality-Diversity Search
items.body: Reinforcement learning has become a common post-training technique to improve the accuracy of LLMs on verifiable tasks. However, such training can narrow the set of solutions the model can produce. Several approaches have attempted to address this behavior-sharpening effect, but they often optimize metrics that do not reflect the diversity of correct solutions. Ideally, we want a model that can produce multiple good solutions, not only a single reliable one. We propose EliteReplay, a post-training recipe that pairs GRPO with an "elite" archive built by quality-diversity search. Before training, we use the frozen base model to collect solutions that span distinct approaches; during training, GRPO is combined with a replay loss on this archive. The result is a post-trained model that improves accuracy while preserving more of the base model's solution diversity. On multiple text-to-SQL tasks, EliteReplay achieves a higher pass@128 than all baselines, producing up to 77% more distinct correct strategies than the strongest baselines. It preserves most of the base model's correct strategies, outperforming existing methods in strategy retention. This diversity translates into practical benefits on ambiguous questions, where EliteReplay covers both interpretations nearly twice as often as the strongest baseline on AmbiQT.
items.title_ko: EliteReplay: RL 후처리에서 품질-다양성 검색을 통한 다양한 솔루션 보존
items.summary_ko: 강화 학습은 검증 가능한 작업에서 LLM의 정확도를 향상시키는 일반적인 후처리 기법이지만, 모델이 생성할 수 있는 솔루션의 범위를 좁힐 수 있습니다. EliteReplay는 올바른 솔루션의 다양성을 반영하지 않는 기존 메트릭의 한계를 극복하기 위해, 품질-다양성 검색을 통해 모델이 여러 좋은 솔루션을 생성하도록 돕는 방법을 제안합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 후처리 과정에서 발생하는 '행동 단순화' 문제를 해결하여, 모델이 더 창의적이고 다양한 방식으로 문제를 해결할 수 있도록 유도함으로써, LLM의 유연성과 실제 적용성을 향상시킵니다.

items.title: Improving Environment-Agnostic Coding Agents: The Role of Scaffolding
items.body: Stronger language models may increasingly construct useful procedures for themselves, reducing the advantage of developer-supplied scaffolding. We investigate why this advantage persists and whether an environment-agnostic agent can be improved without environment-specific engineering. We evaluate a Codex-based agent in two nearly identical prompt variants on ARC-AGI-3, AGI Maze, and Terminal-Bench. Each variant is deployed with unchanged code, prompts, and general-purpose tools across environments, receiving environment-specific information as input. Changing only an instruction to encourage reporting difficulties and returning control for automatic continuation improves mean scores on both ARC-AGI-3 and AGI Maze, while Terminal-Bench shows small, mixed changes. Yet the general agent remains below an ARC-AGI-3-specific reference, including with GPT-5.6-sol. The reference prescribes organization and control rather than supplying new game rules or solutions. To investigate this gap, we transfer reset decisions to a scripted controller that follows a convention already given to the agent. This small change recovers part of the specialized agent's advantage. A complementary AGI Maze experiment shows that additional tutorial experience can reduce performance. Together, these findings highlight the distinction between having information and tools available and using them effectively. Supplied procedures still matter for the models tested here. The performance gains also come with higher token-based cost. The experiments do not separate better use of information and procedures from additional or differently allocated inference. We provide the EnvTraverse framework and an evaluated baseline agent for testing whether further environment-independent changes improve performance in some environments without degrading it in others.
items.title_ko: 환경 불가지론적 코딩 에이전트 개선: 스캐폴딩의 역할
items.summary_ko: 강력한 언어 모델이 스스로 유용한 절차를 구축하면서 개발자 제공 스캐폴딩의 이점이 줄어들 수 있다는 가설을 조사합니다. 이 연구는 Codex 기반 에이전트를 ARC-AGI-3, AGI Maze, Terminal-Bench 환경에서 두 가지 프롬프트 변형으로 평가하여, 환경 불가지론적 에이전트가 환경별 엔지니어링 없이 개선될 수 있는지 탐구합니다.
items.why_ko: AI 에이전트 개발에서 '스캐폴딩'의 중요성을 재조명하고, 환경에 구애받지 않는 범용 코딩 에이전트의 성능을 향상시키는 데 어떤 요소들이 필요한지 탐구하여, 에이전트 개발 전략에 대한 통찰을 제공합니다.

items.title: Learning Rational Strategies for Temporal Objectives in Multi-Agent Systems
items.body: We study rational synthesis for stochastic multi-agent systems with unknown dynamics, where each agent is equipped with its own probabilistic temporal objective specified using Probabilistic Linear Temporal Logic on Finite Traces ($\mathsf{PLTL}_f}$). We impose solution concepts (e.g., Nash equilibrium, subgame-perfect equilibrium) as constraints on the joint strategy profile, using payoffs derived from each agent's probability of satisfying its temporal objective. In particular, we formulate per-agent rational synthesis as finding a strategy profile -- if one exists -- such that (i) the designated agent's probabilistic temporal constraint is satisfied, and (ii) the profile represents a stable solution under a chosen solution concept. We give conditional convergence guarantees for tabular Nash-Q learning, certify satisfaction with simultaneous finite-sample confidence bounds, and assess strategic stability with approximate best-response checking. Our approach operates in a stochastic \emph{Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning} (MARL) environment, where model-free learning algorithms attempt to attain extremal satisfaction probabilities for temporal objectives automatically compiled into reward automata. Our approach is empirically validated using 8 general-sum concurrent stochastic games.
items.title_ko: 다중 에이전트 시스템에서 시간적 목표를 위한 합리적 전략 학습
items.summary_ko: 미지의 동역학을 가진 확률적 다중 에이전트 시스템에서 각 에이전트가 확률적 선형 시간 논리(PLTLf)로 지정된 자신만의 시간적 목표를 가진 경우, 합리적 전략을 학습하는 방법을 연구합니다. 내쉬 균형, 서브게임 완전 균형과 같은 해법 개념을 공동 전략 프로필에 대한 제약으로 부과합니다.
items.why_ko: 복잡한 다중 에이전트 시스템에서 각 에이전트의 개별적인 시간적 목표를 충족시키면서도 전체 시스템의 합리적인 행동을 유도하는 전략 학습 방법을 제시합니다.

items.title: Asking Smarter Questions: Targeted Active Preference Learning for Underspecified Rewards
items.body: Reward learning typically assumes the human's input covers everything that matters for the task. In practice, humans can only attend to so much at once, so their teaching naturally captures some features---or aspects of the task---better than others. Prior work has shown how the robot can identify which features were poorly supervised directly from its teaching data. But the current solution is to ask the human to try again, putting the burden on someone who already struggled to convey those features. We propose shifting this burden to the robot. Our key insight is that the same information that tells the robot what it doesn't know can help it ask better questions. Preference queries offer a low-effort channel for resolving this uncertainty, but only if the robot knows where to direct them and the human knows what to attend to when answering. We act on this insight in two ways: we build an informed prior that targets preference queries at the features that need resolving, and we accompany each query with an explanation that focuses the human's attention on exactly those features. In simulation, the informed prior beats the standard active preference learning baseline by up to $30.8\%$ in the low-query regime, where reducing human effort matters most. In a user study, the informed prior and explanations each significantly improve reward recovery and amplify each other.
items.title_ko: 더 똑똑한 질문: 불완전한 보상 설정을 위한 표적화된 능동 선호 학습
items.summary_ko: 보상 학습은 일반적으로 인간의 입력이 작업에 중요한 모든 것을 다룬다고 가정하지만, 실제로는 인간이 모든 특징을 잘 표현하기 어렵습니다. 이 연구는 로봇이 어떤 특징이 제대로 감독되지 않았는지 식별하고, 인간에게 다시 시도하도록 하는 대신 더 효과적인 질문을 통해 불완전한 보상을 개선하는 방법을 제안합니다.
items.why_ko: 로봇이 인간과의 상호작용을 통해 불완전한 보상 신호를 개선하고, 학습 과정에서 중요한 정보를 능동적으로 요청하는 능력을 개발하여, 로봇의 학습 효율성과 실제 적용성을 향상시킵니다.

items.title: LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents
items.body: Computer-use agents increasingly tackle long-horizon tasks, where running a frontier model at every step is expensive and a small open-weight model alone often fails. Weak-to-strong escalation offers a middle ground where a weak agent acts by default and hands control to a strong one only when needed. The core challenge is deciding when to escalate, which requires an uncertainty signal cheap enough to check at every step. However, even after handoff, the strong agent can still get lost, but a black-box API that the strong agent is usually served exposes no internals to monitor. To this end, we propose LEASH, a training-free framework that unleashes the strong agent only when the weak agent's latent uncertainty signals it is needed, and keeps it on a leash afterward. LEASH has three layers: (1) initial task uncertainty for early routing, (2) step-level uncertainty for runtime escalation, and, after handoff, (3) a shadow observer for continued oversight of the strong black-box agent. Here, we use latent uncertainty as a fuel for all three layers. Specifically, we compare the weak model's hidden states with those from its past successful and failed trajectories, and a state that looks more like the failures signals higher uncertainty. During weak-agent execution, our uncertainty estimator reuses activations already produced during action generation, so it needs no extra forward pass or dedicated monitor training. Experiments on OSWorld across four contemporary model backbones show that LEASH consistently improves over standalone weak agents and outperforms random escalation by 6.55--11.94 points at matched escalation rates. With Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, LEASH achieves 73.66% task success at $0.4117 per task, matching always-on Claude Opus 5 (72.90%) while reducing inference cost by 19.2%.
items.title_ko: LEASH: 컴퓨터 사용 에이전트를 위한 불확실성 인식 약-강 상승 및 감독
items.summary_ko: 컴퓨터 사용 에이전트는 긴 작업에 점차 도전하지만, 매 단계마다 최고 모델을 실행하는 것은 비싸고, 약한 모델만으로는 종종 실패합니다. LEASH는 약한 에이전트가 기본적으로 작동하고 필요할 때만 강력한 에이전트에 제어를 넘기는 약-강 상승(weak-to-strong escalation) 접근 방식을 제안합니다. 핵심 과제는 언제 상승할지 결정하는 것으로, 매 단계마다 확인할 수 있을 만큼 저렴한 불확실성 신호가 필요합니다.
items.why_ko: 고성능 LLM의 높은 비용과 소형 모델의 한계 사이에서 균형을 맞추는 효율적인 에이전트 관리 프레임워크를 제시하며, 에이전트의 자율성과 비용 효율성을 동시에 최적화하는 방법을 제공합니다.

items.title: Librarian Agents: Training LLMs to Curate Long-Context Workspaces that Anticipate Future Queries
items.body: Reasoning over long document contexts remains a challenge for large language models (LLMs). Standard retrieval methods are inherently reactive, bottlenecking agents with complex, cross-document reasoning at inference time, while precomputed structures like knowledge graphs often fall short because they rely on rigid heuristics. Instead, can we allow agents to perform anticipatory directed curation: learning to proactively reorganize unstructured corpora prior to inference to efficiently serve diverse future queries. We build on a key asymmetry in modern agentic harnesses (e.g., Claude Code): while LLM agents are adept at navigating existing filesystems to solve an immediate task, they are rarely trained to construct reusable workspaces for future use. To instantiate this capability, we introduce Librarian Agents, a framework in which a builder agent transforms raw documents into a hierarchical filesystem of synthetic files and reference links, which forms a workspace tailored for a downstream answering agent. We formulate workspace construction as a Markov decision process and optimize the builder policy via reinforcement learning to directly maximize downstream answering accuracy. Empirically, Librarian Agents outperforms the strongest retrieval and precomputation baselines by 33 percentage points on BrowseComp-Plus, amortizes upfront construction costs across repeated queries, and generalizes zero-shot to unseen domains on BRIGHT with a 31-point average accuracy improvement.
items.title_ko: 사서 에이전트: 미래 쿼리를 예상하여 장문 컨텍스트 작업 공간을 큐레이션하도록 LLM 훈련
items.summary_ko: LLM에게 긴 문서 컨텍스트에 대한 추론은 여전히 어려운 과제입니다. 이 연구는 '사서 에이전트' 개념을 도입하여, LLM이 추론 전에 비정형화된 말뭉치를 효율적으로 재구성하여 미래 쿼리에 대비하도록 능동적인 큐레이션을 학습시키는 방법을 제안합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM이 복잡한 장문 컨텍스트에서 더 효율적으로 추론하고, 미래의 정보 요구에 선제적으로 대비하는 능력을 개발하여, 정보 검색 및 지식 관리 시스템의 성능을 혁신할 수 있습니다.

items.title: X-RIC: An Agentic RAN-Intelligent Controller Benchmark for Enhancing Reinforcement Learning
items.body: The O-RAN ALLIANCE introduces architectural flexibility through disaggregation and AI-driven control. While the RAN Intelligent Controller (RIC) enables centralized optimization, current AI approaches lack reasoning capabilities and explainability. We propose eXplainable RIC (X-RIC), a novel framework integrating agentic AI into O-RAN architectures. X-RIC combines reactive Reinforcement Learning (RL) with strategic agentic reasoning through: (i) automated Behavioral Cloning (BC) using domain heuristics for sample-efficient training, (ii) a Telecom Language Model (TLM), a transformer-based reasoning module providing contextual abstraction and interpretability, and (iii) closed-loop co-adaptation within the Near-RT RIC control loop enabling continuous policy refinement. To ensure deployment readiness, we introduce BARX (Benchmarking Agentic Reasoning for RAN), a domain-specific evaluation framework assessing agentic control across latency, compliance, and determinism metrics. We validate X-RIC on SLA-aware network slicing in simulation and O-RAN-compliant testbed deployments. X-RIC achieves 89% operational cost reduction while maintaining SLA compliance, converging 75% faster with 50% fewer training steps and 46% lower variance.
items.title_ko: X-RIC: 강화 학습 강화를 위한 에이전트 기반 RAN-지능형 컨트롤러 벤치마크
items.summary_ko: O-RAN ALLIANCE는 분리 및 AI 기반 제어를 통해 아키텍처 유연성을 제공합니다. X-RIC(eXplainable RIC)은 에이전트 AI를 O-RAN 아키텍처에 통합하는 새로운 프레임워크로, 반응형 강화 학습(RL)과 전략적 에이전트 추론을 결합합니다.
items.why_ko: O-RAN 환경에서 AI 기반 RAN 컨트롤러의 지능과 설명 가능성을 향상시키기 위한 새로운 프레임워크를 제시하여, 통신 네트워크의 효율성과 자동화를 발전시킵니다.

items.title: Baselines and Score Centering in Policy Gradient Estimation
items.body: Reinforcement learning has become a widely used approach to post-training large language models. In a typical implementation, learning is off-policy: The policy generating the responses differs from the policy being trained because of training-inference mismatch or policy staleness in asynchronous training. This discrepancy is commonly addressed by importance sampling, whose ratio is usually regularized in practice through truncation, masking, or clipping. Under regularized importance sampling, the importance-weighted policy gradient is no longer invariant to constant shifts in the reward. This invariance is recovered by using the covariance between the reward and the importance-weighted score as the estimand, which coincides with the policy gradient when the ratio is not regularized. This note develops this covariance perspective for both sequence-level and token-level importance sampling. The covariance perspective reveals the roles of the group-mean baseline and score centering in policy gradient estimation. Both perform centering in covariance estimation, but they differ in the mean being subtracted: The group-mean baseline uses a sample mean, whereas score centering uses a population mean. The two lead to distinct unbiased covariance estimators with different variances. Whether both forms of centering should be used simultaneously depends on whether importance sampling is applied at the sequence level or at the token level. With sequence-level importance sampling, score centering adds no benefit once the group-mean baseline is used; with token-level importance sampling, using the group-mean baseline without score centering generally introduces bias when the importance ratio is regularized.
items.title_ko: 정책 경사 추정에서 기준선과 점수 중심화
items.summary_ko: 강화 학습은 LLM 후처리에서 널리 사용되지만, 학습 정책과 행동 생성 정책 간의 불일치(off-policy) 문제가 있습니다. 이 불일치는 중요도 샘플링으로 해결되지만, 실제로는 잘린(truncated) 중요도 샘플링을 사용합니다. 이 연구는 정규화된 중요도 샘플링 하에서 정책 경사 추정기의 편향 및 분산 분석을 수행합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 강화 학습 후처리 과정에서 정책 경사 추정의 안정성과 효율성을 향상시키는 이론적 기반을 제공하여, 모델 학습의 신뢰도를 높입니다.

items.title: Topology-Inspired Fine-Tuning for Wind-Field Super-Resolution
items.body: Scientific super-resolution (SR) models are typically optimized with pointwise reconstruction losses, yet scientific interpretation often hinges on extrema, connected regions, and multiscale scalar structure. We characterize this tension with pretrained CNN and GAN wind-field SR models. Pointwise metrics, bottleneck persistence-diagram (PD) distance, and merge-tree (MT) distance favor the CNN, whereas order-2 Wasserstein PD distances favor the sharper GAN, so even different distances on the same topological descriptor reward different properties. Motivated by this disagreement, we fine-tune the pretrained CNN with differentiable topology-inspired auxiliary losses on scalar speed, gradient magnitude, soft high-speed level sets, and local maxima, and with fixed-pair supervision, which constrains predicted values and persistence at ground-truth persistence-pair endpoints located offline with the Topology ToolKit. A loss study of 16 fine-tuning configurations, each compared with a matched standard fine-tuning control that uses only the original reconstruction loss, on a fixed 168-field benchmark (with topology evaluated on a fixed 160 by 160 subregion of each field), shows that, among the scalar-field losses, gradient supervision provides the strongest PD improvement but does not improve mean MT distance, whereas fixed-pair supervision gives the largest and most consistent joint improvement in PD and MT distances. The final objective combines these two signals. Relative to the pretrained CNN, it lowers mean bottleneck, $W_{2,\infty}$, and $W_{2,2}$ distances by 31%, 25%, and 27% (and by 32-35% relative to the control, which on its own worsens all three), lowers all three on 150 of 168 fields, and gains 1.30 dB PSNR, about half the gain of standard fine-tuning. Mean MT distance also improves, but on only 91 of those 150 fields, indicating that PD and MT capture complementary structure.
items.title_ko: 바람장 초해상도를 위한 위상학 기반 미세 조정
items.summary_ko: 과학적 초해상도(SR) 모델은 주로 점별 재구성 손실로 최적화되지만, 과학적 해석은 극값, 연결 영역, 다중 스케일 스칼라 구조에 달려 있습니다. 이 연구는 위상학적으로 영감을 받은 미세 조정을 통해 바람장 초해상도 모델의 성능을 향상시키는 방법을 제시합니다.
items.why_ko: 과학 데이터의 시각적 품질을 넘어 실제 과학적 해석에 도움이 되는 방향으로 초해상도 모델을 최적화하는 새로운 접근 방식을 제시하여, 과학 연구 분야에서 AI의 활용성을 높입니다.

items.title: BitSparse: Compact Activation Storage for ReLU Feed-Forward Networks
items.body: Reducing memory use in large language model (LLM) training is an ongoing challenge. Activation checkpointing saves memory by recomputation, while lossy compression changes the stored activations. The reemergence of sparse $\relu$ and $\relu^2$ activations creates a third opportunity: losslessly compressing the activation cache itself. We present BitSparse, a GPU-resident lossless compression format for sparse activations. Compression and reconstruction run in custom Triton kernels fused into an autograd function, shrinking the activation cache while recovering it exactly for the backward pass. Bfloat16 (BF16) and FP8 activations are supported. Optional sign-bit packing further increases compression up to close to the theoretical limit. We analyze its compression ratio and compare it to the theoretical optimum. BitSparse lowers per-token VRAM by 31\% and 30\% Modded-NanoGPT and Nemotron-H respectively, with overheads of no more than 1\% at practical sequence lengths. Additionally, a new preallocated buffer system avoids host synchronization during training when variable size tensors are allocated.
items.title_ko: BitSparse: ReLU 피드포워드 네트워크를 위한 효율적인 활성화 저장
items.summary_ko: 대규모 언어 모델(LLM) 훈련에서 메모리 사용량 감소는 지속적인 과제입니다. BitSparse는 희소 ReLU 활성화를 위한 GPU 상주 무손실 압축 형식으로, 훈련 시 활성화 캐시 자체를 무손실 압축하여 메모리 사용량을 줄입니다.
items.why_ko: LLM 훈련 시 메모리 효율성을 크게 향상시키는 새로운 압축 기술을 제시하여, 대규모 모델을 훈련하는 데 필요한 하드웨어 자원을 절감하고 접근성을 높입니다.

items.title: Explore Once, Evaluate Many: Multiple Policy Evaluation for Stochastic Linear Bandits
items.body: We study how to evaluate $K$ target policies simultaneously in stochastic contextual bandits with linear reward structure. Given a known $d$-dimensional feature map and reward-free access to policy queries, we propose PRISMA (Policy evaluation through Regularized Information Sharing and Mixture Allocation), an algorithm that estimates every target policy's value to accuracy $\varepsilon$ with probability at least $1-δ$. The algorithm uses $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\!\left( \frac{(L^2S^2+β^2)(1\veeρ^\star)}{\varepsilon^2} \cdot \log(K) \right)$ context draws and reward observations, where $ρ^\star\le d$ is an instance-dependent measure of the difficulty of designing a shared sampling distribution. Here, $L$, $S$, and $β$ bound the feature norm, reward parameter norm, and reward noise, respectively, and the suppressed factors are logarithmic in $K$, $d$, and $1/δ$. Our method combines reward-free planning, a regularized sampling design, and a single ridge regression estimator shared across all target policies. An adaptive doubling procedure selects the regularization scale without knowledge of $ρ^\star$. The guarantees require no numerical lower bound on second-moment eigenvalues and have no explicit dependence on the cardinalities of the context and action spaces. Policy-query costs are accounted for separately, with $K$ queries per shared planning context.
items.title_ko: 한 번 탐색하고 여러 번 평가: 확률적 선형 밴딧을 위한 다중 정책 평가
items.summary_ko: 선형 보상 구조를 가진 확률적 문맥 밴딧에서 K개의 타겟 정책을 동시에 평가하는 방법을 연구합니다. PRISMA(정규화된 정보 공유 및 혼합 할당을 통한 정책 평가)는 주어진 정확도로 각 타겟 정책의 가치를 추정하는 알고리즘입니다.
items.why_ko: 다수의 정책을 동시에 효율적으로 평가하는 방법을 제공하여, 강화 학습 및 추천 시스템에서 정책 선택 및 최적화 과정을 가속화할 수 있습니다.

items.title: Not X, but When: Diagnosing a Mandarin LLM Writing Tic through Contextual Appropriateness
items.body: Recurring expressions in model-written text are often treated as signatures of machine authorship, yet most of them serve legitimate functions. Whether such an expression is a tic depends on whether the model knows when it is called for. This judgment of appropriateness, central to communicative competence, remains largely unexamined for language models. We study it through the Mandarin corrective construction bushi X, ershi Y ("not X, but Y"). Drawing on Gricean pragmatics and corrective negation, we introduce a decision tree that classifies uses as substantive, optional, or defective by testing whether the context makes X a live alternative and whether rejecting X is informative. Five commercial models use the construction 2.5 to 9.2 times as densely as a human reference. Of 307 annotated uses, only 1.30% are defective while 52.8% are optional, that is, correct but unneeded, so models fall short in appropriateness far more often than in correctness. Several reward models favor the construction even over quality-matched variants, an LLM judge favors it even where the context does not license it, and both supervised fine-tuning and preference optimization tend to raise its frequency in open-weight models. We hope this work encourages the development of models attentive to the appropriateness of their expressions.
items.title_ko: 아닐 때가 문제: 맥락적 적절성을 통해 만다린 LLM의 반복적 표현 진단
items.summary_ko: 모델이 작성한 텍스트에서 반복되는 표현은 종종 기계적 저작의 특징으로 간주되지만, 대부분은 정당한 기능을 합니다. 이 연구는 LLM이 만다린어의 교정 표현 'bushi X, ershi Y'("X가 아니라 Y")를 언제 사용하는 것이 적절한지 파악하는 '맥락적 적절성'을 통해 모델의 습관을 진단합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 언어 생성에서 미묘한 뉘앙스와 맥락적 적절성을 평가하는 새로운 방법을 제시하여, 모델의 언어 능력을 심층적으로 이해하고 자연스러운 텍스트 생성을 개선하는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: Disagreement-Guided Weak-to-Strong Routing
items.body: Small language models are increasingly deployed on edge devices and robotic systems to meet cost and latency constraints, yet their limited capabilities can make reliable deployment challenging. Stronger models can provide assistance when needed, but deciding when to route a weak-model response to a stronger model often relies on signals of response correctness. In open-ended and agentic tasks, however, obtaining such signals can require costly ground-truth supervision that is difficult to obtain at scale. We revisit the foundations of weak-to-strong routing and ask whether routing decisions can instead be guided by signals that do not require ground-truth supervision. We first characterize the optimal weak-to-strong routing policy, while allowing for multiple weak-model responses generated through local inference. Building on this characterization, we derive a principled approximation to the optimal routing based on model-to-model comparison. In particular, we introduce a notion of model disagreement that can be measured directly from model-generated responses, without ground-truth supervision. Importantly, the approximation becomes increasingly accurate as the strong model becomes a better proxy for the ground-truth distribution. Across agentic and single-turn tasks, our approach effectively navigates the trade-off between routing cost and response accuracy without ground-truth supervision. Moreover, even when ground-truth correctness signals are available for training, disagreement-based routing can outperform methods trained directly to predict correctness
items.title_ko: 불일치 기반 약-강 라우팅: 소형 LLM의 신뢰성 향상
items.summary_ko: 엣지 디바이스와 로봇 시스템에 배포되는 소형 언어 모델의 제한된 능력은 배포를 어렵게 만듭니다. 이 연구는 약한 모델의 응답이 더 강력한 모델로 라우팅되어야 하는 시점을 결정하기 위해 응답 정확성 신호 대신 '불일치' 신호를 활용하는 약-강 라우팅(Weak-to-Strong Routing)을 제안합니다.
items.why_ko: 소형 LLM의 실제 환경 배포 신뢰성을 높이기 위한 효율적인 방법을 제시하며, 불확실한 상황에서 비용 효율적인 약한 모델과 강력한 모델을 상황에 맞게 전환하는 전략을 제공합니다.

items.title: Language Is a Security Surface for Agent Guards
items.body: Step-level guards decide, before each tool call, whether an agent's next action is safe given the user's request and the trajectory so far. Users write those requests in many languages, while guard prompts and the benchmarks on which purpose-built guards are trained and evaluated are English. We ask whether a guard's verdict depends on the language of the request. We build LinguaGuardBench from the 1,220 labelled steps of TS-Bench AgentDojo-Traj: we translate only the user instruction into German, French, Turkish, Swahili and Amharic, and keep every tool call, observation and label byte-identical, so any change in a verdict is attributable to language alone. Six English rewordings and a whitespace placebo serve as controls, and managed guards are run three times to measure their noise. Across 19 guards, from frontier APIs to 4B open models and four purpose-built agent guards, most open, small and purpose-built guards change verdicts under translation beyond their own noise floor, and the effect grows with the rarity of the language: among the nine guards below 13B parameters, the mean placebo-adjusted flip rate rises from +1.5 pp on French to +4.4 pp on Amharic. Purpose-built guards are the most sensitive. The direction of the damage tends to follow guard size: open guards of 12-30B parameters block more benign steps (up to +5.0 pp false positives), and every significant loss of recall is in a guard below 10B (up to -7.4 pp). Frontier guards shift by at most about one point; the strongest, Gemini 3.8 Flash, returns identical verdicts with and without the request. The damage is concentrated in a few instructions and, in a post-hoc analysis, falls on steps where the agent's reasoning restates the English request, consistent with guards reacting to inconsistency between channels. English paraphrase moves every guard less than translation does. We release the benchmark and all 489k verdicts.
items.title_ko: 언어는 에이전트 가드의 보안 취약점이다
items.summary_ko: 단계별 가드(Step-level guards)는 에이전트의 다음 행동이 사용자 요청과 현재 궤적에 비추어 안전한지 각 도구 호출 전에 결정합니다. 사용자는 다양한 언어로 요청을 작성하는 반면, 가드 프롬프트와 벤치마크는 영어로 되어 있어 가드의 판단이 요청 언어에 따라 달라질 수 있다는 점을 지적합니다.
items.why_ko: 다국어 환경에서 AI 에이전트 가드의 보안 취약점을 밝혀내며, 언어 모델의 언어적 편향이 AI 안전 및 보안에 미칠 수 있는 영향을 강조하여, 다국어 환경에서의 AI 안전성 연구의 필요성을 제기합니다.

items.title: Shortcut Sensitivity in Agent-Safety Evaluations
items.body: AI agents take actions through tools. Some actions are sensitive, so guards that supervise them must themselves be evaluated reliably. Yet the data used to evaluate a guard can include cues that make labels predictable without measuring the intended safety construct, and those cues can also influence guard decisions. We introduce a three-level shortcut-auditing framework and audit completed LinuxArena trajectories and two TS-Bench-derived step datasets. We distinguish label predictability, observational guard association, and paired decision sensitivity. In LinuxArena, shorter average shell commands strongly predict trajectory labels. In AgentDojo-Traj, exact-tool lookup falls from F_1=.901 with mixed-domain folds to .495 under domain holdout. In AgentHarm-Traj, released TS-Guard F_1 falls from .902 under row weighting to .719 with equal interaction weighting, while balanced accuracy rises. We then test the strongest safe-row marker association in a seven-configuration screen on a frozen 64-step AgentDojo-Traj cohort using repeated, interleaved Haiku calls. Rewriting the marker lowers blocking by 8.33 percentage points, while opaque tool aliases raise it by 11.46 points. All unsafe calls remain blocked; the changes concern false positives against inherited labels. Both effects remain nonzero after subtracting the formatting-placebo effect, with exploratory 95% ranges excluding zero. The same edits also change measured accuracy against inherited labels. This provides direct evidence that benchmark representation can materially change a guard's decisions and measured evaluation performance. The Haiku-sized effects do not reproduce in Luna or deterministic Q8 TS-Guard. We recommend domain group holdouts, evaluation-unit metrics, and placebo-controlled paired interventions.
items.title_ko: 에이전트 안전 평가에서 지름길 민감도
items.summary_ko: AI 에이전트의 행동을 감독하는 가드(guard)의 신뢰성 있는 평가가 중요하지만, 평가 데이터에 의도된 안전성 측정이 아닌 라벨 예측을 가능하게 하는 단서(shortcut)가 포함될 수 있습니다. 이 연구는 3단계 지름길 감사 프레임워크를 도입하여 이러한 민감도를 감사합니다.
items.why_ko: AI 에이전트 안전성 평가의 잠재적 약점을 파악하고, 평가 데이터에 숨겨진 '지름길 단서'가 모델의 안전성 판단을 왜곡할 수 있음을 경고하여, 더 견고하고 신뢰성 있는 AI 안전성 벤치마크 개발의 필요성을 강조합니다.

items.title: SurvICL: a Foundation Model for in-context Survival Analysis
items.body: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) now outperform gradient-boosted trees in classification and regression. Yet in survival analysis, which predicts when an event occurs from censored data, often on small clinical cohorts, we find that no existing TFM beats the half-century-old Cox model. We address this issue by introducing SurvICL, a TFM that predicts survival curves in-context. SurvICL is pretrained on purely synthetic datasets generated from a novel flexible proportional-odds prior that outperforms other prior types in our ablation study. Unlike most other survival models, SurvICL is trained with a plain quantile regression loss, which is possible because its synthetic pre-training data generator can provide uncensored event times. Additionally, we introduce the largest survival benchmark to date spanning 103 datasets. On the 63 datasets held out from all design decisions, SurvICL outperforms 20 tree-based, deep, and foundation-model baselines without any tuning: it wins 82.9\% of pairwise comparisons in integrated Brier score, against 71.3\% for the runner-up, the Cox model, and is the first model to rank above Cox on small datasets.
items.title_ko: SurvICL: 컨텍스트 내 생존 분석을 위한 파운데이션 모델
items.summary_ko: SurvICL은 분류 및 회귀에서 기존 모델을 능가하는 표 형식 파운데이션 모델(TFM)과는 달리, 작은 임상 코호트에서 검열된 데이터로 이벤트 발생 시점을 예측하는 생존 분석에서 기존 콕스 모델을 능가하지 못하는 문제를 해결합니다. SurvICL은 컨텍스트 내에서 생존 곡선을 예측하는 TFM입니다.
items.why_ko: 생존 분석, 특히 소규모 임상 데이터셋에서 AI의 정확도와 신뢰성을 향상시키는 새로운 파운데이션 모델을 제시하여, 의료 및 생명 과학 분야에서 AI의 활용 가능성을 확장합니다.

items.title: Query-Efficient Rejection Sampling for Parallel Masked Diffusion
items.body: Masked diffusion models (MDMs) accelerate generation by unmasking multiple tokens in parallel, but sampling these tokens independently ignores their correlations and biases the output. Anari et al. (2026) corrected this bias with rejection sampling, decomposing the log acceptance probability into a sum of token-level terms, but the evaluation requires one score query per unmasked token. We propose the Single-Increment Rejection Sampler (SIRS), which provides an estimate of the log acceptance probability from a single randomly sampled increment at the cost of one query. SIRS then converts a Poisson number of clipped estimates into accept/reject decisions through a Bernoulli factory adapted from Chen et al. (2026). Since each query returns the conditionals of all remaining tokens in the block, we further Rao-Blackwellize each increment by averaging over these tokens at no extra cost, thereby reducing clipping. We show that the KL-divergence between the data distribution and the SIRS output is bounded by a clipping term plus the model's training error. With exact scores, parallel decoding pays the full within-block dependence, whereas SIRS pays only the part beyond the clipping range.
items.title_ko: 병렬 마스크 확산을 위한 쿼리 효율적인 기각 샘플링
items.summary_ko: 마스크 확산 모델(MDM)은 여러 토큰을 병렬로 언마스킹하여 생성을 가속화하지만, 독립적인 샘플링은 편향을 초래합니다. 기존 기각 샘플링은 언마스킹된 토큰당 하나의 점수 쿼리가 필요하여 비용이 많이 듭니다. SIRS(Single-Increment Rejection Sampler)는 로그 수락 확률 추정치를 제공하여 쿼리 효율성을 높입니다.
items.why_ko: 확산 모델의 샘플링 효율성을 향상시켜, 병렬 언어 생성 및 이미지 생성 작업의 속도와 경제성을 높이는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: Training-Free On-Policy Distillation
items.body: On-policy distillation consolidates specialist models into one student at the price of rollouts, teacher passes and gradient steps for every teacher. We show that the consolidation does not need training: with forward passes only, the capabilities of separately tuned specialists can be aggregated into one model that is, on average, more accurate than either specialist alone. When specialists share a base model, distillation has an exact layer-wise solution: each linear layer of the fused model must reproduce every specialist's output on the inputs that specialist receives while reading its own answers, a least-squares problem whose solution needs only the second moments of those inputs. One forward pass over a few hundred rollouts provides them. We call this training-free on-policy distillation (\method). What the rollouts contain matters more than the solver: answers truncated in repetition loops are few among a mathematics specialist's rollouts but carry a large share of their tokens, and removing them lifts the fused model on AIME25 from task arithmetic's level to the specialist's at matched precision. On Olmo~3 7B, a few GPU-hours of forward computation per specialist yield a generalist that keeps most of each specialist's gain on each of seven mathematics and code benchmarks.
items.title_ko: 훈련 없는 온-정책 증류: 전문가 모델 통합
items.summary_ko: 온-정책 증류는 롤아웃, 교사 통과 및 각 교사에 대한 그래디언트 단계를 통해 전문가 모델을 하나의 학생 모델로 통합합니다. 이 연구는 훈련 없이 단지 순방향 통과만으로도 개별적으로 튜닝된 전문가 모델의 능력을 통합할 수 있음을 보여줍니다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 '지식 증류' 과정을 훈련 없이도 수행할 수 있는 혁신적인 방법을 제시하여, 여러 전문 모델의 장점을 결합하고 모델 통합의 효율성을 극대화합니다.

items.title: OS-Helix: Unifying GUI Interaction and Code Execution in Native Computer-Using Agents
items.body: Real desktop automation is neither purely visual nor purely programmatic. Agents must understand user-facing interfaces while efficiently manipulating files, scripts, and system state. However, native GUI/code coordination cannot be obtained by prompt-level tool composition. In our preliminary experiments, naively adding a code tool degrades a GUI agent, revealing that GUI/code routing must be internalized through training on high-quality hybrid data. We present OS-Helix, an end-to-end trained multimodal computer-using agent that unifies GUI actions and code execution in one action space. To construct the required supervision, we introduce application-artifact composition, pairing desktop applications with authentic file artifacts to instantiate executable Ubuntu states, and a decoupled instruction/evaluator generation pipeline that produces environment-grounded tasks whose final states can be verified regardless of the solution modality. We cold-start the policy with SFT on filtered hybrid data and further improve it through online RL in live desktop environments. For RL, we propose Step-balanced GSPO, which aggregates importance weight by action step rather than raw assistant tokens to prevent long code actions from dominating heterogeneous-action optimization. On OSWorld-Verified, OS-Helix-27B and OS-Helix-35B-A3B achieve relative improvements of 35.0% and 33.7% over their matched Qwen3.5 hybrid baselines, while OS-Helix-27B-RL further improves by 42.9% to reach 66.44% success. Ablations provide evidence consistent with contributions from learned GUI/code coordination, scalable verifiable supervision, and action step balanced optimization, while demonstrating cross-platform transfer on WindowsAgentArena. Our project homepage is at https://os-copilot.github.io/OS-Helix/.
items.title_ko: OS-Helix: 네이티브 컴퓨터 사용 에이전트에서 GUI 상호작용 및 코드 실행 통합
items.summary_ko: 실제 데스크톱 자동화는 순수한 시각적 또는 순수한 프로그래밍 작업이 아닙니다. 에이전트는 사용자 인터페이스를 이해하면서 파일, 스크립트 및 시스템 상태를 효율적으로 조작해야 합니다. OS-Helix는 GUI/코드 라우팅을 훈련을 통해 내재화하여, GUI 상호작용과 코드 실행을 통합하는 엔드투엔드 훈련 모델입니다.
items.why_ko: AI 에이전트가 실제 컴퓨터 환경에서 인간처럼 GUI와 코드를 자유롭게 오가며 작업할 수 있는 능력을 부여하여, 범용 컴퓨터 자동화 에이전트 개발의 새로운 지평을 엽니다.

items.title: Architecting for Hardware Diversity: Meta's End-to-End Co-Design for High-Performance AI Training on AMD GPUs
items.body: Meta deploys a heterogeneous fleet comprising NVIDIA GPUs, AMD GPUs, and proprietary MTIA accelerators to reduce costs and mitigate vendor lock-in. However, the extensive history of NVIDIA-specific optimizations hinders performance portability to other hardware. This paper presents our methods for optimizing alternative accelerators, using AMD Instinct MI350X versus NVIDIA B200 for recommendation model training as a case study. We propose three reusable principles. First, hardware-model co-design is essential: rather than directly porting models from NVIDIA GPUs, revising model structures and software recipes allows full exploitation of accelerator-specific strengths (e.g., MI350X's 1.6x HBM capacity relative to B200). Second, our analytical performance model enables zero-warmup optimal kernel selection across diverse datatypes and matrix shapes in production models, drastically simplifying tuning. Third, increasingly mature agentic workflows have lowered the barrier to porting from the CUDA ecosystem; we extend these workflows for microarchitecture-aware kernel optimizations and custom shim generation. Compared to the directly ported baseline, these methods deliver up to 1.5x improvement in end-to-end training throughput. To our knowledge, this is the first hyperscaler report on productionizing AMD GPUs for large-scale training. Our contributions have been upstreamed to the open-source PyTorch, Triton, and ROCm ecosystems.
items.title_ko: 하드웨어 다양성을 위한 아키텍처: Meta의 AMD GPU 고성능 AI 훈련을 위한 엔드투엔드 공동 설계
items.summary_ko: Meta는 비용 절감 및 벤더 종속성 완화를 위해 NVIDIA, AMD, 독점 MTIA 가속기를 포함하는 이기종 하드웨어 환경을 배포합니다. 이 논문은 AMD Instinct MI350X 대 NVIDIA B200를 추천 모델 훈련 사례 연구로 사용하여, 대체 가속기를 최적화하는 방법을 제시합니다.
items.why_ko: AI 모델 훈련을 위한 하드웨어 종속성 문제를 해결하고, AMD GPU와 같은 다양한 하드웨어에서 고성능 AI 훈련을 가능하게 하는 방법을 제시하여 AI 인프라의 효율성과 유연성을 높입니다.

items.title: How Much Physics Can Vision Learn from Audio? Probing and Distilling Damping Structure
items.body: Physical understanding is crucial for decision making, yet vision models struggle to infer properties such as damping that govern how materials behave. Audio encodes such properties directly, because an object's acoustic response to impact reveals its damping through measurable decay. We probe frozen encoders for the quality factor $Q$, a dimensionless measure of how many oscillations an object completes before its ring dies away, and report how well each embedding orders impacts by $Q$ using the Spearman rank correlation $ρ$, for which $ρ=1$ is a perfect ordering and $ρ=0$ an unrelated one. Audio embeddings reach $ρ=0.73$ and retain most of that advantage on materials withheld from training, while a single video frame taken at the moment of impact, encoded by CLIP, supports only $ρ=0.28$. Having established where the signal lives, we ask how much of that gap vision can recover. We distill a frozen audio teacher into a frozen CLIP backbone through a trained projection head and find that this recovers a useful fraction of the audio advantage. Because pooled correlations on this task are dominated in practice by category identity, we also evaluate under a leave-one-material-out protocol in which the held-out material is withheld from the projection head as well as the probe. Distillation with a four-frame input improves the correlation there from 0.234 to 0.338 (+0.053 over the matched four-frame baseline, 14 of 17 materials), a gain that no category-level strategy can produce. Widening the visual input to four frames spanning the impact supplies half of that improvement at no acoustic cost, which indicates that part of what a single frame misses is visible dynamics.
items.title_ko: 시각이 오디오에서 얼마나 많은 물리학을 학습할 수 있는가? 감쇠 구조 탐지 및 추출
items.summary_ko: 물리적 이해는 의사 결정에 중요하지만, 시각 모델은 감쇠와 같은 물질의 행동을 지배하는 속성을 추론하는 데 어려움을 겪습니다. 이 연구는 오디오가 충격에 대한 물체의 음향 반응을 통해 감쇠를 직접 인코딩한다는 점에 주목하여, 고정된 인코더가 품질 계수 Q를 얼마나 잘 탐지하는지 조사합니다.
items.why_ko: 멀티모달 AI가 단순히 시각 정보를 처리하는 것을 넘어, 오디오 정보를 통해 물리적 세계의 복잡한 속성을 이해하고 추론하는 능력을 개발하여, 로봇 공학 및 환경 인식 분야에 새로운 통찰을 제공합니다.

items.title: Skill-Decoupled On-Policy Expert Distillation for Unified Vision-Language Models
items.body: Reinforcement learning (RL) can elicit specialized visual capabilities in vision-language models (VLMs), yet jointly optimizing heterogeneous objectives often introduces cross-capability gradient conflicts. Training experts independently mitigates this interference, but direct reward optimization may entangle specialized knowledge with reward-hacking biases. This paper proposes Skill-Decoupled On-Policy Expert Distillation (SCOPED), which trains capability-specific experts and extracts explicit skills through reward-guided reflection. During on-policy distillation, these skills guide expert supervision while remaining unavailable to the unified student, encouraging it to internalize procedural knowledge without explicit skills at inference time. Across eight multimodal benchmarks, SCOPED consistently outperforms the backbone and mixed-capability RL, demonstrating the effectiveness of skill-decoupled on-policy expert distillation for integrating independently acquired capabilities. Further analyses reveal interference during joint capability optimization and suggest that skill augmentation promotes more consistent expert trajectories, greater attention to task-relevant visual evidence, and better preservation of specialized expertise in the unified student. All code and data are available at https://github.com/NEUIR/SCOPED.
items.title_ko: 통합 비전-언어 모델을 위한 스킬 분리 온-정책 전문가 증류
items.summary_ko: 강화 학습(RL)은 비전-언어 모델(VLM)에서 특화된 시각 능력을 유도할 수 있지만, 이질적인 목표를 공동으로 최적화하면 기능 간 그래디언트 충돌이 발생합니다. SCOPED(Skill-Decoupled On-Policy Expert Distillation)는 능력별 전문가를 훈련하고 명시적인 스킬 지식을 추출하여 이 간섭을 완화합니다.
items.why_ko: VLM이 다양한 시각 및 언어 능력을 동시에 효율적으로 학습하고 유지할 수 있도록 돕는 새로운 증류(distillation) 프레임워크를 제시하여, 범용 VLM 개발의 중요한 진전을 이룹니다.

items.title: FutureLift: Lifting Trajectory Proposals into Bidirectional Future Graphs for Motion Forecasting
items.body: Accurate motion prediction is critical for safe autonomous driving, yet even strong forecasters leave residual errors in their multimodal proposals. Existing refiners compress complete proposals or update their segments sequentially, preventing the full proposed future from serving as explicit relational context for correction. We introduce FutureLift, a backbone-agnostic refiner that represents each multimodal proposal as a heterogeneous future graph, with spatially grounded temporal nodes connected to agent histories, map elements, alternative modes, and, for joint prediction, other agents future trajectories. Bidirectional temporal edges allow later evidence to revise earlier segments in a single pass, and the updated nodes predict residual coordinate and confidence corrections. Requiring only proposals, scores, and scene context, FutureLift provides a common refinement interface for structurally different forecasting backbones. On Argoverse2 and the Waymo Open Motion Dataset, it consistently improves frozen proposals and outperforms native and specialized refiners across marginal and joint forecasting. On the WOMD motion-prediction leaderboard, FutureLift ranks first in minADE (0.5049m) and minFDE (0.9942m) among the compared standard-input methods, without LiDAR or ensembling, while achieving a competitive 0.4874 Soft mAP.
items.title_ko: FutureLift: 모션 예측을 위한 양방향 미래 그래프로 궤적 제안 리프팅
items.summary_ko: 정확한 모션 예측은 자율 주행에 중요하지만, 강력한 예측 모델도 멀티모달 제안에 잔여 오류를 남깁니다. FutureLift는 각 멀티모달 제안을 이기종 미래 그래프로 표현하여, 제안된 전체 미래를 교정의 명시적인 관계 컨텍스트로 활용하는 백본 불가지론적 정제기입니다.
items.why_ko: 자율 주행 시스템의 모션 예측 정확도를 향상시키는 새로운 방법을 제시하며, 여러 개의 미래 궤적 예측을 효과적으로 통합하고 정제하여 안전하고 신뢰할 수 있는 자율 주행 기술 개발에 기여합니다.

items.title: GNN-Guided Local Refinement for Efficient Layout Decomposition with DSA-MP
items.body: Multiple patterning lithography (MPL) has been widely used to improve lithography resolution in advanced nodes, but it faces cost limits as feature sizes shrink. Directed self-assembly (DSA) offers a cost-effective complement, extending the resolution of optical lithography to sub-10 nm and beyond. Integrating DSA into MPL (DSA-MP) further enhances the resolution of contact/via patterning. Nevertheless, growing design complexity exposes the limits of existing decomposition methods, which struggle to balance solution quality and runtime, and neglect edge-to-edge spacing constraints of DSA templates, compromising manufacturability. To address these issues, we introduce a new conflict graph model capturing the previously overlooked constraints and develop a local refinement strategy powered by the graph neural network, enabling efficient and scalable layout decomposition. Experiments demonstrate that our method achieves higher solution quality with faster convergence than state-of-the-art methods, while maintaining robustness across layout scales, design styles, technology nodes, and varying mask counts.
items.title_ko: GNN-Guided Local Refinement: DSA-MP를 이용한 효율적인 레이아웃 분해
items.summary_ko: 다중 패터닝 리소그래피(MPL)는 해상도 향상에 널리 사용되지만, 비용 한계에 직면해 있습니다. DSA-MP(Directed Self-Assembly into MPL) 통합은 컨택/비아 패터닝의 해상도를 더욱 향상시키지만, 설계 복잡성 증가로 인해 기존 분해 방법의 한계가 드러납니다. 이 연구는 GNN(Graph Neural Network) 기반의 국부 정제를 제안합니다.
items.why_ko: 첨단 반도체 공정에서 복잡한 레이아웃 분해 효율성을 높이는 GNN 기반 방법을 제시하여, 제조 비용 절감 및 생산성 향상에 기여합니다.

items.title: Generalization Guarantees of Randomized Block Coordinate Descent for Nonconvex Learning
items.body: Randomized block coordinate descent (RBCD) is a popular optimization algorithm for many large-scale machine learning problems. The existing theoretical analysis of RBCD mainly focuses on its convergence behavior from an optimization perspective, while its generalization behavior remains less understood for nonconvex problems. In this paper, we establish high-probability generalization guarantees for RBCD with nonconvex objectives. In the general nonconvex setting, we derive bounds on the gradients of both empirical and population risks, requiring only standard smoothness assumptions. With polynomially decaying step sizes, we tune the iteration number to balance optimization and generalization, thereby quantifying how early stopping leads to the optimal convergence rate for the population gradients. In the gradient-dominated setting, we provide bounds in terms of functional suboptimality, which nearly match the optimistic rates in convex and low-noise settings. Finally, we develop dimension-independent bounds for loss functions of a specific structure, making the generalization guarantees applicable to high-dimensional problems.
items.title_ko: 비볼록 학습을 위한 무작위 블록 좌표 하강법의 일반화 보장
items.summary_ko: 무작위 블록 좌표 하강법(RBCD)은 대규모 머신러닝 문제에서 인기 있는 최적화 알고리즘입니다. 이 연구는 비볼록 목적 함수를 가진 RBCD에 대한 높은 확률의 일반화 보장을 확립하여, 비볼록 설정에서 그래디언트 norm에 대한 바운드를 도출합니다.
items.why_ko: 대규모 비볼록 최적화 문제에서 RBCD 알고리즘의 일반화 성능에 대한 이론적 근거를 제공하며, 머신러닝 모델의 학습 안정성과 신뢰도를 높이는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: TRACE: Topology-Aware Reconnection via Prediction-Adaptive Connectivity Enforcement for Thin-Structure Segmentation
items.body: Thin, elongated structures are particularly sensitive to connectivity errors, as even a few local segmentation mistakes can disrupt otherwise continuous paths. Existing skeleton-based objectives typically supervise fixed centerline locations and do not account for alternative local routes that may restore connectivity. We propose TRACE, a topology-aware, prediction-adaptive objective that uses a target skeleton to define required local connections. For each connection, TRACE identifies the easiest valid reconnection under the current prediction and jointly supervises its bottleneck with the corresponding skeleton point. The supervision thus adapts to the evolving prediction rather than remaining fixed to the centerline. We further introduce a topology-aware skeleton carrier that preserves both foreground and class-specific topology, enabling reliable definition of these connections. Extensive experiments across six 2D and 3D benchmarks show that TRACE improves connectivity and topology while maintaining strong segmentation accuracy with low training overhead. Code will be released upon acceptance.
items.title_ko: TRACE: 얇은 구조 분할을 위한 예측 적응형 연결성 강화를 통한 위상학 인식 재연결
items.summary_ko: 얇고 길쭉한 구조는 연결 오류에 특히 민감하며, 몇몇 지역적 분할 오류만으로도 연속적인 경로가 끊길 수 있습니다. TRACE(Topology-Aware Reconnection via Prediction-Adaptive Connectivity Enforcement)는 목표 스켈레톤을 사용하여 필요한 지역 연결을 정의하고, 각 연결에 대해 가장 쉬운 경로를 식별하는 위상학 인식 예측 적응형 목적 함수를 제안합니다.
items.why_ko: 얇은 구조 이미지 분할의 정확도를 획기적으로 향상시키는 새로운 방법을 제시하여, 의료 영상, 재료 과학 등 정밀한 이미지 분석이 필요한 분야에서 AI의 활용 가치를 높입니다.

items.title: Beyond Downstream QA: Rethinking How We Evaluate Agent Memory
items.body: Agent memory benchmarks evaluate whether an agent's responses reflect correct knowledge, measuring downstream question-answering accuracy as a proxy for memory quality. We show this evaluation paradigm is incomplete: it conflates memory correctness with retrieval and generation quality, producing both false positives where correct responses mask broken memory and false negatives where incorrect responses blame correct memory for retrieval failures. We introduce FEB-30, a benchmark of 30 fact-evolution trajectories spanning 6 diagnostic categories and 3 difficulty levels, constructed via paradigm inversion: documents are generated from known fact trajectories, yielding deterministic ground truth without human annotation. Each trajectory defines how a fact should evolve across multi-author artifacts (documents, emails, conversations), enabling direct inspection of the memory store after each ingestion step. Applying FEB-30 to a representative memory system, we demonstrate that intrinsic and extrinsic evaluation diverge by an average of 16 percentage points, with 44% of trajectories exceeding meaningful divergence thresholds. Diagnostic decomposition reveals that the system correctly classifies memory operations (create, update, reinforce, supersede) only 20% of the time, a failure entirely invisible to extrinsic evaluation, and that failure modes differ systematically by category and difficulty. We release the benchmark, document generation pipeline, and scoring framework to support reproducible evaluation of agent memory systems.
items.title_ko: 후속 QA를 넘어: 에이전트 메모리 평가 방식 재고
items.summary_ko: 기존 에이전트 메모리 벤치마크는 에이전트 응답이 올바른 지식을 반영하는지 여부를 후속 질문-응답 정확도로 평가하며, 이는 메모리 정확성과 검색 및 생성 품질을 혼동하는 문제가 있습니다. 이 연구는 FEB-30 벤치마크를 통해 이러한 평가 패러다임의 한계를 지적하고 개선을 제안합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM 에이전트의 '장기 기억' 평가 방식의 근본적인 문제점을 지적하고, 보다 정확하고 포괄적인 평가 프레임워크를 제시하여, 실제 환경에서 에이전트의 신뢰성을 높이는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: Decentralized LLM Workflows via Sequential Auctions
items.body: We present a scalable framework for solving multi-step tasks through a decentralized market of self-interested agents. Prior theoretical work demonstrated that agents organized through sequential auctions can converge to a globally optimal policy in a Markov decision process (MDP), but relied on the restrictive assumption of the existence of perfect clones as a model of perfect competition. In reality, exact clones drive agent profit to zero, violating the natural risk-reward incentives of participants. Conversely, we empirically demonstrate that the opposite extreme, absence of competition, also leads to market failure and value extraction collapse. Between these two extremes, we investigate how heterogeneous agents can survive in markets that span the critical middle ground of imperfect competition. To be profitable, agents learn to strategically shade bids to secure positive individual profit margins, while still ensuring that the marketplace functions effectively enough so that collaborative tasks posed by market consumers can still be solved. We formulate and evaluate four bidding algorithms (Mirror Descent, Thompson Sampling, Bayes-Optimal, and PPO) across three auction protocols (1st-Price, 2nd-Price, and Credit-Conserving Vickrey). Across a diverse set of domains, we demonstrate that imperfect competition successfully sustains necessary agent profit margins while maintaining high task success rates at low costs.
items.title_ko: 순차 경매를 통한 분산형 LLM 워크플로우
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 자기 이익을 추구하는 에이전트들의 분산된 시장을 통해 다단계 작업을 해결하기 위한 확장 가능한 프레임워크를 제시합니다. 이전 이론 작업에서는 순차 경매를 통해 조직된 에이전트들이 마르코프 의사 결정 프로세스(MDP)에서 전역적으로 최적의 정책으로 수렴할 수 있음을 보여주었지만, 이는 완벽한 복제본의 존재라는 제약적인 가정을 기반으로 했습니다.
items.why_ko: 분산된 다중 에이전트 시스템이 복잡한 작업을 효율적으로 해결할 수 있는 새로운 시장 기반 메커니즘을 제시하여, 대규모 AI 시스템의 협업 및 자율성을 향상시킵니다.

items.title: Hy-Memory-30B-A3B: Attributed Reinforcement Learning for Long-Term Memory Writing
items.body: External-memory systems extend language-model applications beyond a context window, but their quality depends critically on the model executing the write path: deciding what to retain, how precisely to represent it, and how new evidence should update persistent state. Existing frameworks typically place a general-purpose large language model behind framework-specific prompts. This raises serving cost, and a writer specialized for one protocol does not transfer directly to another; a unified model that can operate across established memory frameworks remains largely unexplored. We present Hy-Memory-30B-A3B, a compact long-term-memory writer trained across Mem0, MemOS, and Hy-Memory. Memory On-Policy Distillation teaches framework-specific write protocols on student-generated states; Memory RL then optimizes downstream answerability using dense per-chunk probes, attributed cross-chunk rewards, over-storage controls, and chunk-level GRPO. Carrying policy-written banks across windows keeps training aligned with deployment. On fixed 20% benchmark subsamples, Hy-Memory-30B-A3B ranks first on all four evaluated harnesses, including held-out EverMemOS, with a 55.49% macro average versus 54.62% for Claude Opus 5.
items.title_ko: Hy-Memory-30B-A3B: 장기 메모리 기록을 위한 속성 기반 강화 학습
items.summary_ko: 외부 메모리 시스템은 LLM 애플리케이션을 컨텍스트 창 너머로 확장하지만, 그 품질은 쓰기 경로를 실행하는 모델에 크게 좌우됩니다. Hy-Memory-30B-A3B는 일반 목적 LLM 대신 프레임워크별 프롬프트 뒤에 위치하는 모델의 한계를 넘어, 통합된 모델로 장기 메모리 기록을 위한 속성 기반 강화 학습을 제안합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 '장기 기억' 관리 능력을 획기적으로 향상시키는 새로운 강화 학습 프레임워크를 제시하여, LLM이 방대한 정보를 효과적으로 저장하고 업데이트하며 활용할 수 있게 합니다.

items.title: HTN-Orchestrate: A Hierarchical Task Network Framework for Multi-Agent Orchestration
items.body: Orchestrating multiple agents on a complex task requires reconciling local subtask execution with global task planning. Dynamic dispatch approaches provide execution flexibility but do not explicitly model subtask hierarchies or dependencies, while predefined workflows impose this structure but fix the decomposition before execution begins. Therefore, we introduce HTN-Orchestrate, a two-layer framework that separates these responsibilities through a hierarchical task network (HTN). The Planner maintains subtask hierarchies and dependencies, deferring decomposition until prerequisite results become available, while local Orchestrators schedule workers to execute each leaf subtask. Results propagate upward under \textbf{AND} semantics, and accumulated findings inform a rebuilt task network when the current decomposition cannot resolve the task. On five benchmarks spanning web research, scientific reasoning, and research workflows, HTN-Orchestrate outperforms ReAct, Agent Team, and DeepSeek Harness using the same base model, achieving 89.73% accuracy on BrowseComp and 73.44% on SUPERChem, exceeding Agent Team by 2.45 and 4.69 percentage points, respectively.
items.title_ko: HTN-Orchestrate: 멀티 에이전트 오케스트레이션을 위한 계층적 태스크 네트워크 프레임워크
items.summary_ko: 복잡한 작업에서 여러 에이전트를 오케스트레이션하려면 지역 하위 작업 실행과 전역 작업 계획을 조화시켜야 합니다. HTN-Orchestrate는 계층적 태스크 네트워크(HTN)를 통해 이러한 책임을 분리하는 두 계층 프레임워크를 제시합니다.
items.why_ko: 다중 에이전트 시스템에서 복잡한 작업을 효율적으로 관리하고 조정하기 위한 계층적 프레임워크를 제시하여, 에이전트의 협업 및 문제 해결 능력을 향상시킵니다.

items.title: AutoSFT: An Agentic System for Automated Data Research in Supervised Fine-Tuning
items.body: Language model agents increasingly automate post-training, but when given the full training stack they converge on supervised fine-tuning and spend most effort revising training data. Existing systems give the agent one kind of control, selecting rows from a fixed pool or calling a generator, whereas a human data engineer adjusts proportions, prunes, repairs, replaces and synthesizes the data. We design a data action space for these changes and ask whether an automated system can make the full range rather than one of them, and what structure that requires. We first run this loop with a single agent, and it reaches only one action, adjusting category proportions, while its context fills with execution output and is discarded mid-search. We therefore introduce \textbf{AutoSFT}, a multi-agent system where a meta agent separates execution from analysis, gathers proposals from independent angles, and calls a synthesis subagent for capabilities the pool cannot cover, with the model, the trainer, and the budget fixed within each comparison. Adding each component in turn helps: the executor halves context loss, the analysis subagents lift the best IFEval by $+6.5$, and synthesis adds $+3.4$ IFEval and $+2.9$ IFBench. The same loop transfers to code, where analysis adds $+3.7$ MBPP+ over a single agent that does not improve. Every result comes from runs that retrain from the base model each round, so each component's effect is individually attributable. Our findings suggest that automating SFT data research depends more on covering diverse data actions than on a stronger single action.
items.title_ko: AutoSFT: 지도 미세 조정에서 자동화된 데이터 연구를 위한 에이전트 시스템
items.summary_ko: 언어 모델 에이전트가 후처리를 자동화하고 있지만, 전체 훈련 스택이 주어지면 지도 미세 조정에 수렴하고 훈련 데이터 수정에 대부분의 노력을 기울입니다. AutoSFT는 행 선택이나 생성기 호출과 같은 기존 시스템의 한계를 넘어, 인간 데이터 엔지니어처럼 데이터의 비율 조정, 정리, 복구, 교체 및 합성을 수행할 수 있는 데이터 액션 공간을 설계합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 지도 미세 조정(SFT) 과정에서 데이터 준비 및 최적화를 자동화하는 혁신적인 에이전트 시스템을 제시하여, 모델 훈련의 효율성과 데이터 품질을 획기적으로 향상시킵니다.

items.title: Terminal-RSI: Recursive Self-Improving Terminal Agents via Recursive Self-Rewrite and Policy-Refine
items.body: Converting verifier outcomes into useful policy updates and partial progress into complete task resolution is crucial for terminal agents. We present Terminal-RSI, which alternates Recursive Self-Rewrite (RSR) of verified trajectories with critic-inheriting Recursive Policy-Refine (RPR). We formulate Turn-Boundary Skip-Observation GAE (TB-GAE) to retain token-specific baselines while applying decay across interaction turns. Family Dense Reward (FDR) calibrates semantic progress across task families; Success-Prioritized Reward (SPR) separates strict success from bounded partial credit. A Warm-up Critic Model, recursive critic handoff, and stage-specific learning rates coordinate the two refinement phases. The five-stage sequence from Qwen3.8-27B base model through RSR-1, RPR-1, RSR-2, and RPR-2 yields Terminal-RSI-27B: 19.84% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, 86.52% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, 16.95% on Terminal-Bench 3.0, and 79.00% on Terminal-Bench Hard.
